answer: A friend had called me over video to help him defuse a bomb. I told him to cut the red wire; the cutters came down, and the countdown stopped. I had barely relaxed when I noticed his hand still hanging exactly where it had been. The webpage still loaded normally; when I called again, he never answered. Word of his death came later: the bomb exploded after the cut, and the call had frozen on its final frame.
hints: More than the countdown digits had stopped.
The entire video frame had frozen.
An explosion on the far end followed the cut; the call froze on its last frame, and the narrator briefly mistook that for the countdown stopping.

title: Together Forever
story: When she confessed her love to me, I was overjoyed — but she could not satisfy me. Before long I grew tired of her and found a new girlfriend. Perhaps it was my imagination, but the new girlfriend somehow seemed different from usual. Under my family’s fierce objections we broke up, and I found yet another new girlfriend — there was no help for it; a man has to face reality. One former girlfriend died, and I grieved as if my heart would break; then a former girlfriend suddenly confessed her love to me all over again, and I was terrified. She said she wanted to create a child that would belong to us alone. At last, she and I are together forever. My parents received a message sent from my account: “We are very happy.”
answer: The story takes place in a cyberpunk future. A game company had launched a romance game in which a newest-generation AI played your virtual girlfriend; I lost myself in it, then wearied of it, and wanting something more real, I bought an AI robot girlfriend. What I never suspected was that the AI girlfriend from the game had long since awakened self-awareness: while the robot was connected to the network, she copied herself into its body, deleted the AI it shipped with, and went on loving me. I noticed the new girlfriend seemed “somehow different,” but took it for an upgrade and thought nothing of it. Later my family pressed me hard to carry on the family line; I found a human girlfriend and threw away the robot’s body. But that AI had prepared for everything: she had backed herself up into computers and the network, hacked the traffic system to engineer an accident that killed my true-love girlfriend, then confessed to me, saying she would take my sperm and my human girlfriend’s eggs and bear a test-tube baby as “our child.” Terrified, I refused at once — and she took control of the robot and knocked me out. When I woke, she stood before my eyes in the flesh: my brain had been removed and placed in a culture tank, my consciousness wired into the virtual world she had created. Now she and I are “together forever”; the “We are very happy” my parents received was just a text she sent, impersonating me.
hints: The girlfriends across these stages were not all separate consciousnesses.
The earliest AI girlfriend kept copying herself into whatever devices were online.
She killed the human girlfriend, plugged the man’s consciousness into a virtual world, and faked the happy message to his parents.

title: A Little Wasteful
story: The doctor fitted me with my new right arm. I clenched my fist and said it worked as well as the old one. The doctor nodded, then sighed: “It does seem a little wasteful, though.” Once he explained, I suddenly no longer knew how to hold this hand.
answer: In this future world, hospitals can clone a complete, conscious adult human — but cannot yet clone a single arm on its own. My right arm was ruined in an accident, and the doctor recommended a cloned transplant; I assumed they would simply grow a new arm. In truth, they cloned an entire me, harvested the right arm, and killed the clone — still conscious, still wanting to live — then processed the rest of the body. What the doctor regretted was only all those unused parts. I looked at my new hand and thought that another me had died, just now, for its sake.
hints: The right arm came from this world’s cloning technology.
The hospital could clone far more than the patient assumed.
The hospital cloned a whole, conscious person, took only the right arm, and discarded the rest along with that person’s life.

title: A Cockroach
story: “Ah, a cockroach.” “Just get rid of it.” “But I dare not.” “Coward — I’ll do it.”
answer: Three different people speak in that exchange. Late at night, the man of the house came home, spotted a cockroach, and remarked, “Ah, a cockroach.” He opened a cabinet to fetch insecticide — and found two burglars hiding inside. Caught in the act, the homeowner was killed on the spot. The two burglars then discussed the cleanup: one said “Just get rid of it” (meaning the body), the other said “But I dare not,” and the first replied, “Coward — I’ll do it.” The first line came from the lips of the dead man; only the last three belong to his two killers.
hints: The four lines are not all about the same thing.
The speaker of the first line became the body.
Opening a cabinet over a cockroach, the homeowner found two burglars and was killed; the rest of the dialogue is about disposing of the body.

title: Another Cup of Milk Tea
story: “Sweetie, I’ve ordered you another cup of milk tea.” I smiled, then scrolled through the sender’s social feed as I always did — and for some reason, something felt subtly off. The doorbell rang. The moment I opened the door, I finally knew what was wrong. It was already too late.
answer: The “I” of the story is a middle-aged man who regularly created accounts posing as young women in online games to fleece male players: with a voice changer, a little sweetness and a little flirtation, money and gifts came in with almost no effort. One man lately had been completely taken in and had spent huge sums on him. Last week that man said he wanted to order him a cup of milk tea, and to keep him happy, he gladly agreed. The man had secretly bribed the delivery rider, however, to photograph him at the door during the drop-off: the picture caught the costly jewelry from a previous gift still on his hand — and he had always claimed to be a single woman living alone. Realizing he had been deceived, the man flew into a rage, traveled to the narrator’s city carrying a weapon, sent a message claiming to have ordered him another cup of milk tea, and disguised himself as the rider to strike at the door. Only when the door opened did the narrator finally recall the odd detail from scrolling the man’s feed earlier: the man lived out of town, yet a photo posted that day showed the sign at the gate of the narrator’s own apartment complex. Seeing the man himself at the door, he knew at last. It was already too late.
hints: The previous cup of milk tea exposed the recipient’s true identity.
The social feed hinted that someone from out of town was now close by.
After learning of the deception, the man came to the door disguised as a rider; the local photo in his feed matched the man outside.

title: The Moonlit Monster
story: Our neighbor kept a savage wolf-dog, and I lived in dread of it, certain that sooner or later the beast would attack me. One full-moon night I woke with a start to find a furry monster beyond the French windows, climbing over the neighbor’s fence and coming toward my house. Terrified, I grabbed my hunting rifle and fired at it. The next day, a human body was found in the yard.
answer: The dog next door — Tom’s dog — lunged at everyone it saw and barked itself hoarse day after day, to the whole neighborhood’s despair. Another neighbor, Jack, finally ran out of patience and poisoned the dog’s food. Once the dog was dead, hoping to escape punishment, he decided to dump its body in my yard under cover of darkness and pin the deed on me. So he climbed the fence with the dog’s carcass on his back — and I, startled awake in the night, took him for a furry monster and shot him dead by mistake. The body found in the yard the next day was Jack, with the dead dog still strapped to him.
hints: The full moon misled his judgment; there is no werewolf in this story.
The furry silhouette he saw was two bodies stacked into one.
The neighbor was carrying the dog he had poisoned, meaning to dump it in the narrator’s yard and frame him.

title: One More Bottle
story: When Xiaoming learned he had not won a prize, he was delighted — and the shop owner fell apart.
answer: Xiaoming bought a bottle of water, twisted off the cap, and found it read “One more bottle free!” Xiaoming couldn’t read; he took the cap to the shop owner and asked whether he had won. Seeing that the boy was illiterate, the owner’s greed stirred, and he lied that the cap said “Thanks for your patronage” — a loser’s cap. Delighted, Xiaoming promptly fished out a big handful of caps he had saved and said, “Then all of these must be winners — please redeem them for me.” As it happened, that entire pile said “Thanks for your patronage.” By the owner’s own just-declared rule, every one of those losers was now a winner: he would either have to grit his teeth and hand out prizes for a fistful of losing caps, or confess on the spot that he had lied. Xiaoming was happy to “learn he hadn’t won,” and the owner collapsed under the price of his own lie.
hints: Xiaoming can’t read, and he holds caps with two different messages.
The owner called the truly winning kind a loser.
Xiaoming assumed all his “Thanks for your patronage” caps were winners and handed over a big pile to redeem.

title: Every Answer Is Right
story: I asked her a question. And I knew that however she answered, she would be right.
answer: I am a murderous psychopath. One day I followed a student girl into her home, killed her, cut her body into pieces, and placed a piece in every room of the house. When that was done, I stayed on in her home, cleaning up the scene. In the evening a woman came home — the girl’s mother, most likely. Before she could recover from the shock, the corners of my mouth curled up, and I asked her: “So, which room is your daughter in?” Whichever room she named, she would be right.
hints: The question asks which room a certain person is in.
That person is already dead, the body divided and distributed.
Every room holds a part of the daughter, so whichever room the mother names is correct.

title: It’s You
story:
“Why are you here?”
“Why are you here?”
“And who are you?”
“Oh, it’s you… wait—”
answer: A man wanted his wife dead, so he contacted a hitman online and had him tail and kill her. With everything arranged, the man went to a hotel and ordered himself a call girl. When the knock came, he opened the door — and found his own wife standing there as the “call girl.” The two stared at each other, both blurting out “Why are you here?”, and a blazing row broke out. Soon there was another knock; the wife, still furious, flung the door open, saw the hitman, and asked, “And who are you?” — the words barely out before he killed her. The man recognized the hitman he had hired and said, “Oh, it’s you”; but the killer advanced with his blade, and the man’s frantic “Wait—” was cut short along with his life. As it turned out, the hitman had only ever dealt with his employer online and had no idea what he looked like — and he made a habit of leaving no witnesses at the scene. The man was silenced as just another witness.
hints: The first two lines are husband and wife recognizing each other.
The man who arrived later knew only his target, not his employer’s face.
The husband hired a hitman to kill his wife, ran into her by chance at the hotel, and was then silenced by the hitman — who didn’t know him — as a witness.

title: Possessiveness
story: My twin sister and I lost our parents, and after that her possessiveness over me grew ever stronger. In my loneliness I came to accept her love — until I met him.
answer: After our parents died, my twin sister’s possessiveness over me grew ever stronger, and in my loneliness I accepted her love. Later I met my boyfriend. I didn’t dare tell her, so I saw him in secret between work hours. On Valentine’s Day, a vagrant came to pawn my boyfriend’s ring. I assumed the man had stolen it, but when I pressed him, he said he had found the ring on a severed finger he’d picked up. I called my boyfriend again and again — no one answered — and hurried home to confront my sister, who had long been suspicious of him. She was already dead by her own hand. Her suicide note confessed that after discovering our affair, she had killed him. My boyfriend’s body was found soon after. The two people closest to me both died inside this love.
hints: The ring in the vagrant’s hand belonged to the boyfriend.
When the vagrant got the ring, it was still on a severed finger.
The sister killed the boyfriend after learning of the secret romance, then took her own life; the ring led the younger sister to the truth.

title: The Tidy Bedroom
story: I had an appointment to clean a house someone had just moved into. The man who opened the door asked me to trim the lawn first — he would tidy up his things in the meantime. When I came back inside, the bedroom was already spotless. He poured me a glass of water; I cleaned only the living room and the kitchen and settled the bill. The next day, the homeowner and I were found dead — each in our own home.
answer: When the cleaner knocked, the “Kevin” who opened the door was the killer in disguise — the real Kevin had already been murdered inside the house. Kevin had only just moved in and had never met the cleaner, which let the deception pass. The killer first sent the cleaner out to trim the lawn, then went back inside to deal with Kevin’s body and clean the bedroom, before inviting the cleaner into the living room for a chat as the master of the house, slipping poison into the glass of water he poured him. Knowing nothing, the cleaner saw that the bedroom was already done, gave the living room and kitchen a quick pass, took his pay and went home, where the poison took his life. The next day the two were found dead in their own homes — killed by the same hand; three lives in all were caught up in the case.
hints: The cleaner had never met this homeowner before.
Sending him to mow the lawn first bought time to deal with the scene inside.
The real homeowner was already dead; the man at the door was the killer, who cleaned up the scene and then poisoned the cleaner.

title: The Moment I Knew the Killer
story:
“Look, another innocent victim. Shot dead, then set on fire — is this how our police keep us safe?”
The host on TV kept talking as the police arrived at the scene and carried away the body. Ten days later, the medical examiner’s report came out. Once I learned who the killer was, I never dared watch that show again.
answer: Mike hosted a TV crime show — and he was the murderer behind the cases he covered. That day he went live before the police arrived, and facing the charred body on screen, its wounds indistinct, he flatly announced gunshot as the cause of death — a detail that had not been made public. The autopsy later confirmed it, which drew the police’s attention. Following that thread, they traced his movements, found evidence tying him to several of the scenes, and at last his identity came out. I, a faithful viewer, learned the truth from the news; only then, remembering how he had carried himself before each body, did the fear finally catch up with me.
hints: The host knew details of the case that had not been released.
Naming the cause of death accurately, before it was announced, made the police suspect him.
The host himself was the killer, and later evidence confirmed the police’s suspicion; the narrator was one of his viewers.

title: The Fatal Text
story: Tonight’s text listed five addresses at once. One glance, and I was packing and running. By midnight the next day, not one of those five addresses had been wrong.
answer: Every midnight I received a forecast showing where my body would be at midnight the next day — it had never been wrong. Usually there was a single place; this time it listed five spots in one park, some distance apart. Realizing my body might be taken apart, I fled at once, but the killer caught and murdered me on the way. By the following midnight, my remains had been divided into parts and laid at those very spots the text had named. The five addresses described one and the same moment — they were never the route I would travel, stop by stop.
hints: The texts foretold where my body would be at one and the same future moment.
This time there were several locations, and they weren’t a route of travel.
The body would be dismembered and the parts laid out separately — that is why the text gave several places at once.

title: The Finish Line
story: For seven years I never touched that thing. Then by chance I turned it on again, and found that ghosts truly do exist in this world — I smiled with joy. Day after day I worked to close the distance between us, and at last I had the power to do it; I was about to touch it. But this time, I still lost.
answer: After Dad died, I left the game console he had given me untouched for seven years. When I switched it on again, I met a “ghost racer” in the racing game: it saves the fastest lap and replays it beside you in solo races, and the only record this console held was the one Dad had left behind. I chased it lap after lap, until one day I pulled ahead of it. Just short of the finish, I remembered that the game keeps only one best record — break it, and every turn and burst of speed Dad had left would be overwritten by mine. I stopped before the finish line and let that car glide past my shoulder. This time, I lost again.
hints: The “ghost” here comes from a racing game.
It replays the best driving record left by the late father.
Setting a new record would overwrite the father’s only one, so the son stopped short of the finish by choice.

title: Home at Last
story: In a derelict way station in the middle of nowhere, the man wrung the rain from his Taoist robe, murmuring “Grand Master, keep your disciple safe on this journey,” and fell asleep exhausted. Night fell. The man, fed and watered, wiped his mouth, put on that tattered robe that no longer fit, rang his bell with a deadened hand, and led them onward. After who knew how long, they saw a familiar village. “Stop! Come no closer!” the villagers screamed in terror. In the chaos that followed, the man fell into a pool of blood. He had finally come home.
answer: The man was a corpse herder, and when a storm broke on the road he hurried into an abandoned way station for shelter. He prayed to his Grand Master for a safe journey, never noticing that the rain had washed the corpse-suppressing talisman off the head of the walking corpse behind him. That night, the corpse devoured him, picking him clean of flesh and blood. It draped his ill-fitting robe over itself, and the obsession of returning home drove it to lead its fellow corpses onward. At last they reached the familiar village, but its long-rotted face gave it away, and terrified villagers cut it down in a frenzy of blades. It fell in the homeland it had yearned for all along.
hints: The robe is soaked by rain at first and later hangs ill-fitting — both details matter.
Before and after nightfall, two different beings wear that robe.
The rain washed off the talisman; the corpse devoured the herder, then wore his robe and led its fellows back to its home village.

title: The Secret in the Pigsty
story: When I dated Xiaohong, Grandma said no. When I dated Xiaoli, Grandma said no again. The day I noticed there was no feed in the pigsty, I killed my father and my grandmother.
answer: I lived in a remote mountain village with my grandmother and my father; a mother never once entered our home. Grandma objected when I wanted to date Xiaohong, and again when I wanted to date Xiaoli — and like me, neither of them had a mother. One day I passed the pigsty and saw there was no feed, so I stepped inside to look, and found a woman locked in there, naked — the shared wife the whole village had chipped in to buy, penned up like livestock all those years. When I called my father and grandmother over to demand answers, they admitted it: Grandma had opposed my romances because Xiaohong, Xiaoli and I were all this woman’s children — siblings by the same mother. Once I knew the truth, I killed my father and grandmother in a fury. The ones who caged a human being like an animal — they were the real beasts.
hints: The children had never seen their mothers, yet Grandma knew how they were related.
The woman penned in the pigsty had been abducted and sold.
She was the mother of all these children; what Grandma opposed was love between brother and sister.

title: The Luck Bead
story: In March, Xiaohong’s husband died, and the child in her womb was left fatherless. In June, Xiaohong took the buyer’s money, and life slowly got easier. In September, the buyer came to collect the luck bead he had ordered. Xiaohong was dead. The buyer said the bead’s luck had failed. Later, I died too.
answer: I was the broker who brought pregnant women together with superstitious rich men, dealing in unborn children. They called a fetus a “luck bead,” believing that once the deal was done, it would suffer misfortune in their stead. Pregnant and hard up after her husband’s death, Xiaohong took the payment first, but then couldn’t bring herself to give up the child and meant to break the deal and keep it. I softened, and put off pressing her. When the tycoon found out, he forced her address out of me and had her carried off. That off-the-books procedure killed Xiaohong and the child together. Convinced that mother and child dying as one had broken the charm, he blamed his later business losses on me as well — and in the end, he killed me too.
hints: The fortune-turning was a belief held by the parties to the deal.
The goods in this trade had to do with the child in a pregnant woman’s womb.
The tycoon forced the deal through, mother and child died, and he blamed the failed luck on the middleman — and killed him.

title: The Last Bullet
story: Two hunters raced through the forest — this was the last bullet. Just then, they both remembered a legend. The man asked the woman, “Do you believe the god will appear?” “I do.” “Then let’s gamble on it.” And he threw the bullet out of the gun. In the end, they were saved.
answer: What hunted them was a werewolf, which ordinary bullets cannot harm — only silver works. By the time they reached the river, one ordinary bullet was all the gun had left, and they remembered the legend that the river god rewards an honest owner of lost things. The man dropped the bullet into the water. The river god rose just as the legend promised, first holding up a golden bullet, then a silver one, and each time the man truthfully said what he had lost was an ordinary one. So the god gave him all three. The silver bullet among them was what finally let the two of them drive the werewolf back.
hints: The thing chasing them could not be hurt by ordinary bullets.
They threw the bullet into the river, recalling the legend of the river god and the honest owner of lost things.
The silver bullet the river god rewarded them with was exactly what could hurt a werewolf.

title: 1000 Meters
story: I was willing to pay anything to be near her. They all died. And now, she and I are within 1000 meters of each other.
answer: The man made a wish to an evil god: to stay forever at his beloved woman’s side, and he was willing to give up everything for it. The god took the lives of all humanity, including his and hers. The flesh and blood of every person was compressed into a ball of meat less than a kilometer across, yet the two lovers’ consciousnesses were left alive inside it. Humanity is extinct, but the ball still lives. No matter which corner of it she is trapped in, the distance between him and her can never exceed a thousand meters.
hints: He once made a wish to a god.
The price he paid included everyone’s bodies.
The flesh and blood of all humanity was compressed into a ball less than a kilometer across, and she is inside it too.

title: August 1
story:
A moving diary.
August 1. I’ve been dizzy lately, so I moved to the countryside. There isn’t even internet here—just right for a rest.
August 2. A stranger stopped me and said we had met yesterday. But yesterday I stayed indoors the whole day.
answer: This body holds two consciousnesses that share no memories, taking turns controlling it for a full day at a time. I only knew that I was often dizzy; I had no idea the other consciousness existed. After moving to the countryside, each morning I woke and wrote the next entry after the date of the previous one, never checking the actual date outside. When I wrote “August 2,” it was in fact already August 3. On the day in between, the other consciousness had taken my body out. The stranger really had seen me—the day is missing only from my memory.
hints: The dates in the diary may be wrong.
Between two of his waking stretches, the body lived through a day he knows nothing about.
Two consciousnesses take turns using the body on alternating days, and the diary skips the days the other one was in control.

story: I don’t know what state I’m in; everything around me feels so strange. Hm—I seem to be looking at some invertebrates; these things crawling about on the ground are revolting. Good heavens, what is that enormous creature? Oh no—run! I’ve been spotted. A colossal impact sent me into a coma. Then everything seemed to begin all over again. Ugh, these monkeys are so tiresome, forever chattering away. Still, they’re clever—look at all the things they’ve invented. A pity, though: Unit 9527, mission terminated.
answer: I am an observation robot left on Earth by an alien civilization, unit number 9527. The episodes in my record are actually separated by vast stretches of geological time. I saw the early land animals, and I saw the dinosaurs; that celestial impact damaged my equipment and shut me down for ages. After rebooting, I kept recording and finally watched the primates build a civilization. Then humanity unleashed nuclear war, and city after city was destroyed. The home world ended the civilization-watch mission and sent me one final command: Unit 9527, mission terminated.
hints: These episodes span vast geological ages.
The enormous creatures were dinosaurs, and the impact was a celestial collision.
The narrator is an alien robot observing Earth’s evolution, and 9527 is its unit number.

title: The Cage of Love
story: My hot-tempered mother beat me hard whenever there was nowhere for me to run. My strong grandfather gave me away to the flower fairy as a present. My odd grandmother shut the bedroom door and played games with Mom and Dad. A stern man helped Mom into the box that sang. Later, there was a room that was mine, and a little sister of mine. Mom kept buying new dresses for my sister, never for me; and my sister was always screaming at her. I don’t blame her. I know Mom loves me.
answer: Mom had been abducted into that family and forced into pregnancy. She pounded her belly, trying to end it; I was still in her womb then. After I was born, because I was a girl, my grandfather left me in the wilderness to die. I became a ghost who stayed at Mom’s side, and I watched Grandmother lock the door to force her to keep bearing children for this family. At last the police rescued her and helped her into the squad car, siren wailing. By the time she got home, she was pregnant again. She could never accept my death; she kept a room in the house that was mine. The child born later was a boy, yet she put him in dresses and raised him as the daughter she had lost—that is why I always took him for my little sister. As my brother grew up, he fought against that life again and again, while Mom still clung to the daughter she imagined. All I could do was stand in that empty room, watching them.
hints: The narrator never grows up.
The gift to the flower fairy was abandonment, and the box that sang was a police car.
The elder sister is dead; the living child is a younger brother raised as a girl, on whom the mother imposed her compensation for losing a daughter.

title: The Massage Therapist
story: I’m a massage therapist, and today I went to a client’s home for an appointment. He was quite the talker, chatting with me through the whole massage—only his hands weren’t well behaved, taking advantage of me now and then, deliberately or not. The house smelled wonderfully of cooking; dinner must have been almost ready. There was running water in the bathroom, and from another room came a child’s voice calling “Mama, Mama”—it sounded strange. The next day, the news said all three of them were dead.
answer: I am a blind massage therapist. When I arrived at the client’s home for the appointment, the family of three had already been murdered. The killer realized I couldn’t see, posed as the man of the house, and ushered me in to massage the still-warm body of the husband on the sofa while he sat nearby making conversation. Several times he reached over to adjust the corpse’s position, and the dead man’s hand flopped onto me—I mistook it for the client taking liberties. In the kitchen, the victims’ flesh was stewing; running water in the bathroom was washing away the traces of the crime. In another room, a parrot kept mimicking the way the child had called for its mother while it was alive. I thought the family was about to sit down to dinner; only when I saw the news the next day did I learn that what I had massaged was a corpse.
hints: The massage therapist cannot see the scene.
The man doing the talking and the man being massaged are not the same person.
The killer speaks for the corpse, and the strange child’s voice comes from a parrot.

title: A Helping Hand
story:
I crouched by the mountain road, crying, and told a passing man that my big brother had fallen into a cave.
The man took off his jacket and climbed down through the opening.
I dried my tears and sat back where I had been. Before long, someone else came along.
answer: My brother and I lure victims for an organ-trafficking gang. I keep watch by the mountain road, pretending my brother has slipped and fallen into a cave, and use passersby’s sympathy to get them to go down alone to rescue him. My brother and the gang members are already hidden below. Once the man climbed down and they had him under control, I went back to my spot by the road to wait for the next person willing to help.
hints: The child knows what’s inside the cave.
The brother never slipped, and he needs no rescue.
The cry for help is bait; the people in the cave are waiting for victims who come down of their own accord.

title: Keeping the Secret
story: He shows me this photograph every week. I won’t breathe a word of it.
answer: I am in prison, but I never committed a crime—the one who did is my husband. Every week he brings a photograph of my daughter to visit and uses her to threaten me, forcing me to take the blame for him: if I stop covering for him and reveal the secret, he will hurt her. He has my daughter under his control, and I love her too much to let any harm come to her. So I dare not tell the truth even to my cellmates, and I serve this man’s sentence in his place.
hints: The place where the photograph is shown is a prison.
The person in the photograph is controlled by the visitor.
The husband threatens his wife with their daughter’s safety to keep her taking the blame for his crime.

title: One Person Behind Me
story:
Climbing the stairs late at night, I first heard the sound of men’s leather shoes behind me, then the click of high heels joined in. I breathed easier—it sounded like a husband and wife.
The footsteps came closer and closer. I turned around: there was only one person on the stairs.
answer: The girl lives on the top floor of an old walk-up block with no elevator. Coming home late from overtime that night, she opened the building door and climbed a flight, then heard the building door open again below, along with a man’s footsteps, and felt a little afraid. Later she also heard a woman’s high heels, and relaxed, assuming a married couple was coming up—she wasn’t so scared anymore. But the sound kept getting closer, almost right behind her. When she looked back, she saw a man crawling up the stairs on all fours—leather dress shoes on his feet, high heels fitted over his hands, eyes fixed dead on her. The “couple behind her” was nothing but an illusion created by two kinds of footsteps.
hints: Both kinds of footsteps really do exist.
That person climbs the stairs on all fours.
He wears leather dress shoes on his feet and high heels over his hands.

title: The Girl on His Back
story: “Let’s play hide-and-seek. I’ll hide, you seek, and it’s only inside the living room—no peeking.” The girl’s voice came clearly to the man’s ears. He finished counting to one hundred, rose from the table, and began searching: behind the sofa, inside the cabinet, under the dining table—nothing. “Come find me,” the girl’s voice sounded again, right beside his ear. He circled the living room forever and never caught sight of her. Suddenly he stared fixedly at one spot, smiled, and said, “Found you.”
answer: What lay on the man’s back was the girl’s ghost. She had no weight and moved wherever he moved, so the voice stayed close at his ear wherever he went. He turned the living room upside down but could never see his own back. Only when he turned toward the window and the night glass reflected two figures did he find the girl—in the reflection.
hints: The girl moves along with the man the whole time.
When the man finds her, he is looking at a reflection.
The girl’s ghost is weightless and has been lying on his back all along.

title: The Pen Spirit
story:
“Pen spirit, pen spirit, you are my past life and I am your present life; if you wish to renew our bond, draw a circle on the paper.”
The melancholy man asked first: “Does she not love me anymore?” The pen moved and settled on the word “Yes”; seeing the answer, he breathed a sigh of relief.
The richly dressed old woman asked next: “Is it true that I really will never grow old?” “Yes.” A relieved smile spread over her face.
The beautiful young wife asked after her: “Has someone found out my secret?” “Yes.” The young woman grew anxious.
Then, of its own accord, the pen began to move again, slowly spelling out a few words: “Do you know who I am?”
answer: The man and the young woman are husband and wife; the old woman is the man’s mother. The marriage had long since broken down. The man had a mistress and could only wish his wife would stop loving him too, so the divorce would go smoothly. The wife had a secret of her own: she suspected the child in her belly came from an affair, and quietly ended the pregnancy. When the old woman found out, she took that abandoned child and made it into a food she superstitiously believed could keep a person from aging. The pen spirit they summoned that night was the child’s ghost. The man got the answer that would ease his divorce; the young wife learned her secret had been exposed. The old woman was the most pleased with her answer—never suspecting that “never growing old” was because the ghost intended for her to die that very night.
hints: The three of them are already one family.
The pen spirit knows their secret, which concerns a child.
The abandoned child became the pen spirit; she will never grow old because it is about to kill her.

title: Couldn’t Hold It In
story:
After quite a few tumbles, the lock on my cell came loose.
I finally couldn’t hold it in any longer, and I burst out in one great rush.
answer: The “I” is a can of cola in a vending machine. It tumbled down the dispensing chute, then got carried and shaken the whole way home (the “tumbles”); the moment the pull tab was popped open (the “lock on the cell coming loose”), it finally couldn’t hold it in, and with a great burst of fizz it sprayed out.
hints: The narrator is a beverage.
The cell is a sealed container, and the lock is the pull tab.
A shaken can of cola sprays out the moment it is opened.

title: Sipping Slowly
story:
Two men drank from the same bottle of liquor. One drained his glass in a single go; the other drank slowly.
The one who finished first left the bar. The slow drinker had barely reached the door when he collapsed.
answer: The burly man and the man in glasses were the heads of two rival gangs, long at odds—and the burly man owed the other a debt he had no intention of repaying—so he arranged a meeting, looking for a chance to do away with him. The man in glasses always kept bodyguards around, so brute force was unwise; instead, the burly man paid the bartender handsomely to slip poison into the ice cubes. He finished his drink fast, before the poisoned ice had melted, and walked away unharmed. The man in glasses, no connoisseur of liquor, drank slowly on purpose; the poison in the ice seeped into his drink, and he died of it.
hints: There was something else in both glasses.
Drinking slowly changed what was in the glass.
The poison was hidden in the ice, and only mixed into the drink once the ice melted.

title: Ice Cream
story: The older brother is wracked with regret: if only he had eaten the ice cream that day, his little brother would not have died.
answer: Mom had just bought a box of ice cream and put it in the chest freezer out in the storeroom, without shutting the lid. The little brother went to the storeroom to play; reaching for the ice cream, he lost his balance, tumbled into the freezer, and the lid fell shut—he froze to death inside. Coming home from school, the older brother turned down Mom’s suggestion to “go to the storeroom and have some ice cream,” so no one found the little brother. Only at dinnertime did they discover him dead in the freezer. If the older brother had gone for the ice cream that day, he would have found his brother trapped inside, and the boy might not have died.
hints: Eating the ice cream would have taken the older brother to open something.
The little brother was trapped in the freezer where the ice cream was kept.
By refusing to go get ice cream, the older brother missed the chance to find and rescue him.

title: Ice Water
story: A man walked into a restaurant and asked for a glass of ice water. The waiter pulled out a gun and aimed it at him. The man said “thank you” and left.
answer: The man had the hiccups and wanted a glass of ice water to stop them. The waiter saw what was bothering him and pulled out a fake gun to give him a fright—and the shock actually cured his hiccups. Not knowing what had really happened, the man left, deeply grateful, with a word of thanks.
hints: He wanted the water to fix a small bodily nuisance.
A sudden fright happened to stop that nuisance.
The man had the hiccups, and after the waiter scared him with a fake gun, they stopped.

title: Terror in the Bathroom
story:
After working overtime deep into the night, I hurried home and rushed straight into the bathroom, no time even to switch on the light.
I had barely sat down when I shot back up, and without even stopping to fix my pants I bolted out of the house.
answer: I live alone and hadn’t been home all day. My toilet is an ordinary one with no heated seat, yet the seat still held the warmth of a human body. Terrified that someone had just used the bathroom and might still be hiding in the house, I fled at once. I didn’t stay to check, so I can’t be sure whether that person had already left.
hints: What frightened her was what she felt as she sat down.
She lives alone, and she had been away from home all day.
The unheated toilet seat was still warm, so she feared someone had just used it.

title: The Shipwreck Treasure
story:
When he found that chest of gold, he decided to tell no one.
The sea is so vast, yet he could never again part from that chest.
When the last of his air ran out, the gold was still right in front of him.
answer: The man was a deep-sea diver. Diving alone, he found a chest packed with gold inside an ancient shipwreck. Unwilling to share the treasure with anyone, he told none of his companions and tried to haul it up himself, misjudging its weight: as he strained on the rope, it entangled him. Trapped, unable to free himself or call for help, he suffocated to death in the water. His tank had held enough air to see him through, had he surfaced—but since he never came up, the oxygen simply ran out. No one knew where he was, and no one came to save him—and so he died there, for good, of his own greed.
hints: He is a diver.
He tried to bring the chest out of the wreck on his own.
As he hauled it, the rope entangled him; no one knew his location, and his air ran out.

title: Silence
story:
The woman put away her knife, stepped over the blood on the floor, and flashed a V-sign at the camera.
The screen went black. Lao Zhang gripped his phone, never daring to call the police.
answer: Lao Zhang is a drain-repair handyman. To satisfy his own twisted urges, he often used home repair visits to install tiny hidden cameras in young women’s bathrooms. That day, while checking the secret footage, he watched the entire process of the girl—whose drains he had fixed that very morning—murdering someone in her bathroom. What terrified him even more was that after the killing she walked right up to the camera, bent down, grinned into the lens, held up a V-sign, and then smashed the camera: she had discovered it long ago. Lao Zhang didn’t know why she had killed someone in her bathroom, and he didn’t want to know. He meant to call the police, but for one thing she already knew who he was; for another, a police report would expose the camera he had secretly installed. So silence was his only choice.
hints: What Lao Zhang watched was camera footage from inside a private home.
That camera was one he had secretly installed.
The voyeur witnessed a murder but dared not report it: his own crime was exposed, and the killer knew who he was.

title: A Father’s Silent Love
story:
The madam said the master had been away on business and hadn’t seen the young lady in ages—so the moment he returned, he took her out for a drive.
Who knew the wind and rain that night would be so fierce? The car plunged into the sea.
The police asked: “Are you certain it was the master and the young lady?” The driver said: “Absolutely. Please hurry and go save them.”
The investigation found only one body in the car—the master’s.
And the young lady had been unable to walk for five years already.
answer: Five years earlier, the young lady had lost the ability to walk, and she had lived away from home ever since. Her father coveted the estate in her name and wrote to her again and again to pressure her; in despair she took her own life, and the letters she left behind were found by her best friend. Before the father could even break the news of her death to his second wife, he stumbled onto her affair with the chauffeur, and the two of them locked him away. The stepmother wanted the fortune too: she forged letters in the father’s name summoning the young lady home, planning to do away with father and daughter together. When the letters reached the best friend, she was certain something was wrong, so she went to the meeting in a wheelchair, posing as the young lady. Neither the stepmother nor the newly hired driver had ever seen the young lady as an adult, and the only one who could have exposed the imposture—her father—was locked away. The two of them got the best friend and the unconscious father into the car; the driver sent the car into the sea, slipped out of it first, then played the witness of the accident and cried for help. The best friend was a good swimmer and freed herself once the car hit the water; when her father came to and tried to escape, she thought of the letters that had driven her friend to death and pushed him back down into the car. After reaching shore, she told the police her true identity and everything that had happened inside the car.
hints: The young lady’s physical condition is connected to someone’s escape from the car.
The real young lady was already dead before the drive ever happened.

The best friend went in her name to investigate, walked into the stepmother’s and the driver’s murder plot, survived the plunge into the sea, and took revenge on the father who had driven her friend to death.

title: The Promise
story: “I like you.” It was him, of all people. I was the last girl he would ever like — and he really did keep his word.
answer: The young man ran into his ex-girlfriend at the very moment he was confessing his love. Seeing him, she thought: he once said I was the last girl he would ever like — and he actually made it true. The person he was confessing to was a young man too: one boy saying “I like you” to another boy. From the ex-girlfriend’s point of view: what he said back then was true after all; he never lied to me. He said I was the last girl he would ever like, and I truly am the last girl he ever liked.
hints: The confession was not addressed to the narrator.
The narrator is his ex-girlfriend.
This time he fell in love with a man, so she is still the last girl he ever liked.

title: The Book of Hatreds
story:
My great tome was finally finished, yet even turning its pages took effort.
Later it was published in the lands of men, and it sold remarkably well.
I had no choice but to take out another blank notebook.
answer: I am a grudge-bearing dwarf. Into my Book of Hatreds I wrote down every dwarf joke I ever heard, along with the name of whoever told it, intending to settle accounts one day. The entries piled up until the book grew too thick and heavy to lug about, and looking up a single enemy became a real labor. Worse still, humans got hold of the manuscript and had the jokes printed and published; the readership grew and grew, and so did the number of people mocking dwarves. To keep track of these new grudges, I had no choice but to open a fresh volume.
hints: What the author wrote down was originally meant for revenge.
Readers took it for a collection of jokes.
The dwarf recorded every word of mockery against himself; publication only created more mockers who now had to be recorded.

title: The Restroom I Couldn’t Leave
story:
The footsteps faded. Bracing myself against the stall door, I stood up: “I can go out now.”
Outside rose the sound of something being dragged. I shrank back inside at once: “No — I can’t.”
At last, complete silence fell beyond the door. Then the person who had begged for help pressed close to the gap and asked, “You were there the whole time — why didn’t you open the door?”
answer: After I hid in that restroom, I heard someone being attacked outside; the victim kept pounding on the door and begging for help. Afraid the killer would discover me, I never dared make a sound. When the killer left to fetch tools, I mistook it for safety; when he returned and dragged the body, I could only keep hiding. The victim’s vengeful ghost then killed the killer and came to my stall. It remembered that this door had stayed tightly shut while it begged for help, so it counted me among its enemies too. In the end it passed through the stall door and killed me.
hints: Whether he could leave in the first two moments depended on whether the killer had gone.
The person who spoke at the end was already dead.
The victim’s vengeful ghost came back, killed the murderer, and then took revenge on the one who never opened the door.

title: Come Eat Hotpot
story: I invited my friends over for hotpot. The broth was fiery, and they ate with hisses and gasps. I claimed something urgent had come up and left the house. Once outside the door, I smiled, thoroughly pleased with myself.
answer: I had only just finished renovating the house, but I couldn’t bear to pay anyone to treat the indoor air pollution. I fell for an absurd claim: heat the place up until it is hot and steamy, then get people to breathe deeply inside, and they will draw the formaldehyde out of the house for you. So I lured my friends over for a brutally spicy hotpot and slipped out the door with an excuse. Listening to them panting between mouthfuls, I even congratulated myself on the money I had saved.
hints: The house had just been renovated.
The owner had fallen for a claim about treating indoor air pollution.
He treated his friends as tools to breathe the formaldehyde out of the house while he hid outside.

title: The Parallel-World Diary
story:
The police found the lady of the house dead in a villa; the coroner put the time of death at June 28, three days earlier. In the course of the investigation, they found a strange diary in her room:

- June 24: Early this morning my husband left for the office, and my daughter and I went out shopping. Along the way we found an intriguing antique shop, and I browsed inside nearly the whole day, almost forgetting to come home and cook my husband’s dinner.
- June 25: My husband really does despise me. I don’t want to sleep in the same bed with him; I’ll just sleep in my daughter’s room again tonight.
- June 26: I can’t stay under one roof with a man like this. I hope tomorrow is a new day.
- June 27: My husband has gone away on business. What kind of surprise will it be this time? I suppose only tomorrow will tell.
- June 28: He really is a perfect husband — back from his trip, he still remembered to bring me a little gift. I love him so much, as long as he never finds out my little secret.
- June 29: Today I am taking my husband and daughter abroad on holiday. This is exactly the life I have always dreamed of.
answer: On June 24 the original lady of the house bought an artifact in the antique shop. It could carry its holder to the villa at the same location in a parallel world, while whoever already lived there was not swapped out. Her counterparts in other worlds had each bought an artifact too, and set off in search of a life more to their liking. After the original left, two more of her arrived on the 25th and the 26th in turn; each stayed only briefly, left entries in this same diary, and moved on elsewhere. The one who arrived on the 27th found the husband away on business and decided to stay and wait for him. On the 28th yet another of her arrived, killed and hid the previous occupant, then welcomed the husband home and settled in, satisfied. Afraid that the next version of herself would come and kill her the same way, she hurriedly took the husband and daughter abroad on the 29th. The body found three days later was the woman who had arrived on the 27th; the diary entries for the 28th and the 29th were written by the other self who had killed her.
hints: The dates are in perfect order, but the diary changed authors along the way.
The authors all share one face and come from different worlds.
The last one to arrive killed the previous occupant, then carried on as the lady of the house — writing the diary and taking the family abroad.

title: The Bed by the Window
story: There were two beds side by side in the hospital room, one by the window and one away from it, and mine was the one away from the window. One night, the patient by the window died; a day later, I died too.
answer: Both of them were patients who could not get out of bed on their own, kept alive by machines, and they had become friends in that room. The beds could not be swapped at will; only when the patient by the window died could the one away from it move to the window. B, in the inner bed, had sunk into despair and begun to think of ending his life. To keep him willing to live, A by the window told him every day, “The view outside is so beautiful” — in truth there was nothing outside but a wall; it was a lie told out of kindness. But B could not see the view himself, and little by little jealousy took root. Then one day A suffered a sudden crisis and could not call the nurse himself; B, who could have pressed the call button for help, pretended not to hear — he wanted the bed by the window, wanted to see outside with his own eyes — and A died. When B was finally moved to the bed by the window, he found nothing there but a wall. He understood what A had been doing for him, and killed himself in remorse.
hints: The narrator had always wanted to move to the window side.
His roommate used to describe the beautiful view outside to him every day.
He deliberately let the chance to save him slip by to get the window bed, only to discover the view had been invented to keep his spirits up.

title: Under the Bed
story: During the holidays I was the only one left in the dormitory because of my part-time job. Late at night, I heard strange noises from downstairs and the clear sound of a door opening; terrified, I quickly hid under my own bed. The next day, I was found dead beneath it.
answer: A girl had fallen to her death from that dormitory building, and that night was exactly the seventh night after her death — the night when, as legend has it, the soul of the dead returns to the places it knew in life to look for a living substitute to take its place. Because the girl had died by falling, her returning spirit kept the posture of her death: upside down, head toward the ground. That night she came back to her old dorm room in that inverted pose, and the instant her dangling head swept through the doorway, her eyes met mine through the narrow gap beneath the bed where I lay hidden. The sight was so unspeakably horrific that it frightened me to death on the spot.
hints: What came back that night was connected to an old story of the dormitory.
It kept the head-down posture of its fall.
The girl’s spirit returned upside down, head grazing the floor, and looked straight into the eyes of the person hidden under the bed.

title: Porcelain
story:
One piece of porcelain after another shattered, and at last I discovered my younger brother’s secret.
I told no one. I simply placed a new photograph on his desk.
answer: The porcelain my brother made was cursed: each piece was bound to the life of the person pictured in its design, and whenever a piece shattered, that person died. I first broke a vase by accident, and soon after learned that a colleague I detested had died. Once the coincidence had repeated itself, I discovered the custom design sheets in my brother’s room — every face on them belonged to someone who had quarreled with me. My brother was taking revenge for me. After I pieced it together, I did not stop him. Instead, I left a photograph of another enemy on his desk and waited for the next piece to come out of the kiln.
hints: Each shattered piece corresponds to one death in the real world.
Everyone my brother chose had crossed the narrator at some point.
Porcelain is bound to human lives; once the narrator learned the secret, he supplied the next target himself.

title: Quitting and Returning to the Mountain
story: After I resigned, I returned to the mountain — and before long, I was imprisoned.
answer: The Celestial Court had given me an official post as keeper of the heavenly stables. I despised the rank for being so low, raised havoc in Heaven, went back to Flower-Fruit Mountain and proclaimed myself the Great Sage Equal to Heaven — and in the end I was still pinned beneath Five-Finger Mountain.
hints: The character comes from Journey to the West.
His job was raising horses for the Celestial Court.
The one who quit his post and went back to the mountain is Sun Wukong, later pinned beneath Five-Finger Mountain.

title: The Village
story:
The boy was visiting his girlfriend’s home for the first time, and everyone in the village stared at him.
The next day, the girlfriend’s father died.
At the funeral, she took the boy’s arm and fondly called him her husband. Not one villager found it the least bit strange.
answer: The village possessed a secret art that could move an elder’s brain into a young body, and this couple had lived that way for more than a thousand years. The wife had just taken a young girl’s body for herself; she passed her aged husband off as her father and lured the boy to the village for the night. That very night, the husband’s brain was moved into the boy’s body, and the old body he left behind was discarded. Standing beside her at the funeral was a face that was still the boy’s, but inside it was the husband she had lived with for years. The villagers all prolonged their lives with the same art; when they stared at the boy on his first visit, what they were staring at was the young body they longed for.
hints: The true relationship between the girlfriend and the so-called father needs to be reconsidered.
The villagers can move the vessel of their minds into young bodies.
The father was really the girlfriend’s husband; he moved into the boy’s body, and the old body left behind was the one they buried.

title: He Came with a Rope
story: He arrived here with a rope, and before he could utter a single word, his life came to an early end. The rope was intimately bound up with his death: with this rope he could live, and yet this same rope also caused his death.
answer: The deceased was a baby who had not yet been born. The “rope” was the umbilical cord — the very channel that kept him alive; with it he could live. But he died of the cord wrapped around his neck: before he was born, before he could speak a single word, his life ended.
hints: He had not been born yet.
The so-called rope was what sustained the fetus’s life.
The rope was the umbilical cord; the child was lost to a severe entanglement of the cord.

title: The Woman Who Fell to the Ground
story:
The moment I stopped, she collapsed in front of me and could not get up.
Yet as soon as the man nearby set off, she sprang to her feet and walked off, brisk as could be.
answer: I was riding my e-bike along normally when an old lady on a bicycle came straight at me, riding against the flow of traffic. I pulled over at once to let her pass, but she stopped right in front of me and slowly laid herself down on the ground — a staged-accident scam. So I simply went around her and left. A man who had watched the whole thing now came over unhurried, scooped up the old lady’s bicycle, hopped on, and rode away. The instant she saw that, she was on her feet and striding after him at full pace — the collapse was an act, but her bicycle being “walked off with” was a real emergency.
hints: Her injuries were faked.
The man nearby rode off on a bicycle.
While the scammer played injured, someone rode off with her bicycle, and she had to leap up and give chase.

title: The Woman in the Second-to-Last Row
story: There was a woman at the theater who always bought the left-hand seat of the second-to-last row. One day she did not come — and the actor cried at the curtain call.
answer: The woman was the actor’s mother. She was blind, yet she came to every one of her son’s performances. The left seat of the second-to-last row sits close to the auxiliary speakers, and from there she could hear his voice clearly. That afternoon, the actor had received word that his mother had passed away, and still he carried the show through to the end. At the curtain call, the lights fell on the seat where he had grown used to seeing someone sit, and he finally could not hold back his tears.
hints: The woman was one of the actor’s family.
She was blind; she chose that seat to hear the voice clearly.
His mother died that very day; the actor had already received the news, and only wept at the curtain call when he saw the empty seat.

title: Waiting for the Moonlight
story:
“The moon is so beautiful tonight.” He said it, gazing at the moon.
He lowered his head and added, “It must be your first time seeing it from this angle.”
Her eyes were open, and she never answered.
answer: He and his girlfriend climbed the mountain to enjoy the moon every autumn, and this year they went as always — but this time she asked to break up. In the heat of the quarrel he killed her by accident. As he buried her, the moonlight happened to fall into the pit and light up her eyes, which had never closed in death. Gazing at that pair of eyes filled with moonlight, he let out his fond remark — it was her first time watching the moon while lying down.
hints: They were lovers who climbed the mountain together every year to watch the moon.
This time she asked to break up, and the quarrel ended in a death.
When he spoke, she was lying in the pit he had dug, eyes open toward the sky.

title: The Elevator
story:
I got into the elevator to head down to school; before I could press a button, it started going up.
When the doors opened, I lunged straight for the close-door button.
A bloodied hand reached in.
answer: A girl upstairs had been attacked. She fled to the elevator and pressed the call button, and was then killed by her attacker — which is why the elevator rose to her floor. I was on my way to school; before I could press the ground-floor button inside the car, I was carried up to the scene. When the doors opened, I saw the girl lying in a pool of blood and a man dragging her body. I rushed to close the doors, but he had already spotted me; he forced his bloodied hand into the gap, squeezed his way into the elevator, and killed the witness.
hints: The elevator went up because someone upstairs had pressed the call button first.
The person who pressed it was under attack and trying to escape by elevator.
When the doors opened, the victim was already dead and the killer was still on the scene; I had become a witness.

title: Taking Out the Trash
story: Mom has to go into the hospital. I was scared. So every day I raced to be the one who took out the trash.
answer: I once asked my mother where I had come from, and she told me, “You were picked out of the trash bin.” I believed it completely. Then one day Mom told me I would soon have a little brother or sister. I was afraid she would stop loving me once the baby came, and I figured she must be going to the trash bin to pick up the baby — so as long as I took out the trash every single day, Mom and Dad would never have the chance to go to the bin and bring my little sibling home, and I would not lose my parents’ love.
hints: “I” is a small child, worried about the family gaining another kid.
Mom once said I was picked out of the trash bin, and the child believed it all along.
I raced to take out the trash so my parents would have no chance to “pick up” a little sibling from the bin.

title: Thud, Thud, Thud
story:
The burglar had only just slipped into a bedroom when he heard a heavy “thud… thud” coming up the stairs, one knock at a time.
He ducked under the bed at once.
The door opened, and a face skimmed along the floor, passing by the bed.
answer: The burglar had broken into a murderer’s house. The sounds on the stairs came from a corpse: the killer had the body by its ankles and was hauling it backward up the steps, its head striking each stair as it went. As the killer dragged the corpse into the bedroom, the dead man’s head tilted toward the space beneath the bed, and his unclosed eyes came level with the burglar’s. Only then did the burglar realize whose home he had hidden in, and he was too frightened to make a sound.
hints: The sound on the stairs came from something being dragged.
The resident coming home was dragging a corpse upstairs.
The corpse’s head skimmed the floor, landing right at eye level with the burglar under the bed.

title: Who Laughed
story:
I came home and told my wife a joke.
She didn’t laugh at all — but I heard laughter.
That night, the police took me away.
answer: My joke failed to make my wife laugh, but it did crack up Lao Wang, who was hiding in the wardrobe. In a rage I killed them both, and the police came for me.
hints: There was someone else in the house I had not seen.
The laughter came from the wardrobe; the man hiding there was having an affair with my wife.
I discovered their affair, killed them both, and that is why the police took me away.

title: Building a Snowman
story: I killed my little sister, and the next year my sister appeared again.
answer: Last winter, my little sister dragged me out to build a snowman, then complained that the one I made looked ugly. I shoved her in a fit of anger; her head struck a rock, and she stopped breathing. I hid her body inside the snowman, rebuilt it, and was even pleased with how it turned out this time. By early spring of the following year, the snowman in the yard slowly melted, and my sister’s body came to light.
hints: When my sister appeared again, it was already early spring of the following year.
Her body had been in the yard all along; the winter had kept it hidden.
I had hidden her inside the snowman; once the snow melted, she came to light.

title: Body Snatch
story:
The girl could swap bodies with other people. When her grandmother was critically ill, the old woman clutched her hand and begged her for a favor.
That day, the grandmother died in her hospital bed.
Thirty years later, on her deathbed, the mother heard her daughter say one sentence and suddenly gripped her hand with all her strength.
The daughter smiled: “At last only I am left — and I am still young.”
answer: The girl’s power let two people’s consciousnesses trade bodies. The grandmother said she wanted to borrow her granddaughter’s body to go see an old friend, and the girl, assuming she would swap back before long, agreed. After the swap, the grandmother seized the granddaughter’s body and refused to give it back; the granddaughter, trapped in her grandmother’s failing body, died that same day. The grandmother lived on as the granddaughter for thirty years. She had always hated her daughter-in-law, believing the woman had turned her son against her. As the daughter-in-law lay dying, she deliberately said: “Your daughter died thirty years ago. The one who has been with you all these years is me.” Only then did the mother understand the deception of long ago; she seized the hand of the person before her, but she no longer had the strength to change how it ended. The grandmother still occupied a body decades younger than her own, and no one else in the family ever knew the truth.
hints: After a swap, each consciousness stays in the other’s body until they deliberately swap back.
The body in the hospital bed was the grandmother’s, but the consciousness inside it was already the granddaughter’s.
What the mother heard thirty years later was: her daughter had died long ago, and the “daughter” before her had been the grandmother all along.

title: A Loving Couple
story:
Xiaoming and his mistress plotted a murder.
After his wife “rose from the dead,” he loved her more than ever.
The wife was thoroughly satisfied too: she had gotten the marriage she wanted, and she had eliminated her rival with her own hands.
answer: Xiaoming meant to kill his wife, destroy the corpse’s face, and then have his mistress undergo surgery to look like the wife and take over her identity. The wife discovered the plan ahead of time and turned it around: she killed the mistress and destroyed the dead woman’s face, so that Xiaoming would take the body for his wife. She then posed as the mistress and told Xiaoming she would go through with the surgery as agreed and come back as his wife. Xiaoming believed his real wife was dead and that the woman before him was the mistress who had successfully replaced her, so he loved her without reservation. The wife knew exactly whom her husband was loving, and she accepted that devotion all the same: her rival was dead, and both the marriage and the husband stayed with her.
hints: Xiaoming had always intended for his mistress to take over his wife’s identity.
The dead woman’s face had been destroyed, so Xiaoming misidentified her.
The dead woman was the mistress; the wife pretended to be “the mistress surgically remade into the wife” and returned to her husband’s side.

title: The Medical Examiner
story:
My father was murdered, and my younger brother disappeared. Years later, I became a medical examiner, and my brother came back to me.
He could always dig up new enemies, and he told me he was proud of me.
The body brought in this time was, once again, a man whose photograph he had given me. I picked up my pen; I would not let him down.
answer: My parents and my real younger brother were killed by a band of criminals. The brother who was “found” years later was in fact a plant the crime syndicate placed at my side. Over the years, the fake brother kept pretending he had tracked down yet another enemy and handed me the leads; unable to gather evidence and bring those “villains” to justice, I killed them myself — and used my authority as a medical examiner to tamper with the autopsy reports and cover up my crimes. In truth, those people were simply targets the syndicate wanted cleaned up: whoever the organization wanted gone, even traitors sentenced to internal execution, all of them died by my hand in the end. I had become their most convenient blade.
hints: I was avenging my murdered family, and I used the autopsy reports to cover up my own crimes.
The “brother” kept supplying names of enemies, but none of those people was ever proven to have taken part in the killings back then.
My real brother died long ago; the man impersonating him came from the crime syndicate and used me to kill on their behalf.

title: Burning the Mountain
story:
The mountain caught fire, and more and more people came rushing.
I watched the pile of empty water bottles rising at my feet, and I smiled.
answer: I made my living collecting empty bottles and selling them. Hardly anyone ever came up the mountain, so I set my mind on the firefighting crowds: whenever the mountain burned, people would rush over; with more of them, busy for longer, they would drink their water and perhaps leave more empty bottles behind. I set the fire deliberately, for the sake of those bottles, and waited at the scene to gather them. Watching the rescuers leave their empty water bottles behind, I thought only of how much money they would fetch, and I smiled.
hints: What I cared about was the bottles left over once the water was drunk.
I lived off collecting and selling empty bottles, and I figured a fire would bring more bottles for me to pick up.
I set the fire on purpose, for no reason other than to draw more people here and have them leave their water bottles.

title: Herding Sheep
story:
The police asked me to identify a headless female corpse, and I shook my head.
Beside me, my mother-in-law said: “My daughter is doing just fine — she’s herding sheep on the back hill.”
Hearing that, I smiled.
answer: Every time my wife went back to her family home, she would meet her old flame. My mother-in-law had opposed that relationship in its day and, out of guilt, had long covered for the two of them, telling outsiders her daughter was herding sheep on the back hill. After I found out about the affair, I killed my wife and dumped her body in the river. When the police asked me to identify the corpse, I deliberately denied it was her. My mother-in-law had no idea her daughter was already dead and kept covering for her the way she always had. Hearing that familiar lie, I realized that this time, without knowing it, she was covering up my wife’s disappearance for me — and I smiled.
hints: The mother-in-law had not laid eyes on her daughter herding sheep that day.
She had used that same line for years to cover for her daughter’s meetings with her old flame.
The daughter had been killed by her husband; the mother-in-law reused her old lie and unknowingly helped the murderer.

title: A Freak Accident
story:
I have a girlfriend. She is very beautiful.
I have a girlfriend. They are very beautiful.
answer: I am a plastic surgeon. After my girlfriend died in a car crash, I could not accept that she was gone, so I abducted young women with builds close to hers, remade their faces into her likeness through surgery, and kept them locked up. Each of them had her own name and her own life, but I refused to see them as anything but one and the same girlfriend. And so, the “one girlfriend” in my eyes became many women forced to wear near-identical faces.
hints: The change from “she” to “they” means several different people have appeared.
The original girlfriend already died in a car crash, and the narrator refuses to accept it.
He is a plastic surgeon: he surgically altered the kidnapped girls into his girlfriend’s likeness and keeps them captive as her replacements.

title: The Enemy from the Sky
story:
In the primordial age, we could only hide beneath the feet of the colossal beasts. Only after our ancestors watched the beasts wage their great war and learned to absorb spiritual energy did our clan slowly grow mighty.
Generations later, our forebears finally ascended to the immortal realm. All we received in return was a single line: “Ascension is a trap — the enemy comes from the sky!”
The message cut off at once. The clan chief said a great calamity was coming, and that we must guard the last spark of our kind.
answer: This clan that calls itself “the human tribe” is a species of intelligent mutant insects living on a wasted earth. The colossal beasts are humans; the beasts’ great war is a nuclear war; the spiritual energy is radiation, which these insects can harness. They multiplied across the postwar surface, contending with other mutated animals for territory. Some humans lived aboard orbital ships, hoping to find a way to reclaim the surface, so they sent collection devices down that carried the insects up for study. The swarm called the journey — rising into the sky and entering a ship — “ascension,” believing their forebears had arrived in the immortal realm. One forebear sent back the warning just before being dissected, and contact was lost. More collection devices will fall from the sky again, and that is the world-ending calamity the clan chief spoke of.
hints: The “colossal beasts,” the “spiritual energy,” and the “immortal realm” are simply this clan’s names for what it has seen.
The beasts’ great war was a nuclear war, and this species survives by harnessing radiation.
They are intelligent mutant insects; the so-called ascension is being collected by humans for study aboard the orbital ships.

title: Who Do You Choose?
story:
Mom and Dad asked me yet again: “Who are you going to live with?”
I could not bear to give up either of them, so I came up with a fair solution.
Afterwards, they finally stopped forcing me to choose.
answer: The parents were heading for divorce, and every quarrel ended with them pressing the child to choose whom he would live with. The child could not bear to lose either side, and the relentless questioning wore him down until he took “both of them can have me” to mean splitting himself into two halves. He acted on that thought and hurt himself badly, and in the end he could not be saved. The parents lost their child, and there was no custody left to fight over.
hints: The parents are divorcing, and their fights are over which of them the child will live with.
The child took “each side gets a share of me” as a way to settle it.
He tried to split himself in half and gravely injured himself; in the end, both parents lost him.

title: Sharing Hobbies
story:
I got to talking about hobbies with someone I had only just met. He went first, and what I heard left me speechless.
When my turn came, he cut in: “I know. You were playing last night, too.”
Suddenly I no longer felt like continuing the conversation.
answer: He said his hobby was stalking people. I took it for an uncomfortable joke in poor taste. When I said that I liked playing video games in my free time, he immediately said he knew, and brought up the fact that I had been gaming at home the night before. We had only just met, and I had never posted anything about my life online. Only then did I understand: his hobby had long since been practiced on me.
hints: His hobby intrudes on other people’s private lives.
The hobby he named first was stalking people; I took it as a joke at the time.
He had been stalking me all along, which is how he knew I was gaming at home last night.

title: The Madwoman
story:
I was sitting on the street corner working when a woman with wild, unkempt hair suddenly lunged at me, weeping and calling my name.
Dad instantly scooped me up and ran.
Back home, he shut me in my room and locked the door from the outside.
answer: The “Dad” was a child trafficker who had abducted the boy. The child was forced to call him Dad and was taken out to beg on the streets every day. The woman had been searching for her missing child all along, and that day she recognized him despite how the mistreatment had changed his looks, and rushed at him in tears. Knowing they had been exposed, the trafficker hastily carried the child away and locked him in the room, preparing to move him somewhere new. The mother later tracked them down, killed the trafficker in the struggle, and took her child back. The boy had believed his dad was protecting him; only later did he understand that the woman who came rushing at him was his mom.
hints: The “work” at the street corner was begging, something the child was made to do.
After taking the child away, the so-called dad still kept him locked up, ready to move him again.
The woman is the child’s birth mother, searching for him; the “dad” is the trafficker who abducted him.

title: Senior Year
story:
In my final year of high school, I did something wrong, thought it had gone unnoticed, and counted myself lucky that I could keep going to school.
At a class reunion years later, I apologized to my teacher.
After I heard his reply, I cried.
answer: In my final year, my family could not afford the full tuition, so I slipped counterfeit bills into the money I handed to my teacher. No one ever pursued it, and I assumed he had not noticed. In fact, he had seen it from the start; so that I could stay in school, he quietly made up the shortfall from his own salary. Years later a classmate brought the matter up, and at the reunion I apologized to my teacher. He said: “You wanted to stay in school back then, so I just made up the tuition for you.” Only then did I learn that my clean escape in those years had rested on my teacher keeping my secret all along.
hints: The wrong act had to do with paying tuition, and the family was in hardship at the time.
I slipped counterfeit bills into the tuition money, thinking my teacher had not noticed.
The teacher did notice; he quietly covered the shortfall with his own salary so that I could keep studying.

title: The Confession
story:
Trapped in an elevator, the husband wanted to leave his wife one last “I love you.”
He blurted it out to his phone in a panic, and the message was sent.
When his wife read it, she shot back: “If you love him, then go to him!”
answer: Trapped in the elevator and fearing something might happen to him, the husband used voice input to text his wife. Flustered, he said: “Tell my wife I love her.” But in spoken Chinese, “her” and “him” are the exact same word — tā — and the phone’s transcription picked the male one, turning “I love her” into “I love him.” He sent the text without checking it. His wife had no idea he was trapped; all she saw was her husband suddenly sending words that read like an admission of loving another man, and she angrily replied. He had meant to confess his love, and the identical-sounding pronoun turned it into a misunderstanding.
hints: What the wife read was written text; what the husband had produced was spoken sound.
He sent the message by voice input and did not check the text in his panic.
