In spoken Chinese “her” and “him” sound identical; “I love her” was transcribed as “I love him,” and the wife thought her husband loved someone else.

title: Shine My Shoes
story:
He ducked into an alley, pulled off his jacket, and walked back out unhurried.
The police ran right past him.
He stopped at the curb: “Give my shoes a shine.”
The shoe-shiner looked up at him: “He’s the one.”
answer: He was the jewel-store robber. Spotted by the security guard during the robbery, he killed the guard and bolted into the alley to change his outfit. His shoes had hidden lifts in them; with the jacket swapped, the appearance and height the witnesses had noted no longer matched the man before them, and the pursuing officers ran past without recognizing him. Yet he could never bring himself to give up that specially made pair of leather shoes. The guard’s family watched the surveillance footage over and over, memorizing the shoes’ distinctive seam pattern and their old repair marks, then set up nearby posing as a shoe-shiner to wait. The day he sat down for a shine, the family member saw the same telltale features up close, recognized the suspect, and immediately alerted the police; the follow-up investigation confirmed who he was.
hints: He was evading pursuit: he changed his jacket in the alley but never changed his shoes.
The clue the shoe-shiner knew came from surveillance footage of a murder at a jewelry store.
The shoe-shiner is a relative of the slain guard, waiting specifically for that pair of leather shoes with their distinctive repair marks to appear again.

title: Stay Close to the Grown-ups
story:
Mom said that crossing the road is safe as long as you follow a grown-up.
There was no traffic light that day, so I walked close behind a man.
He didn’t stop, and neither did I. Neither of us ever reached the other side.
answer: I had just started first grade. My parents were busy with work and had me walk to school by myself. Mom instructed me that at intersections without traffic lights, I should cross together with a grown-up. I always believed that grown-ups judged the safety first. But the man that day had already resolved to end his life; he was carrying a suicide note and walked deliberately into the onrushing traffic. Knowing nothing of his intent, I kept following right behind him, and both of us were killed in the accident. The following that used to reassure me had led me straight into a danger a grown-up had chosen for himself.
hints: The child assumed every grown-up crossing the road was judging whether it was safe.
That man was carrying a suicide note, and his purpose was entirely different from the child’s.
The man walked into the traffic on purpose to end his life; the child, not knowing, followed him and died in the same accident.

title: The Bus
story:
I stood by the handrail of the bus. The cabin was cold, and a stench of rot hung in the air, never dispersing.
One after another, they came toward me, and not one of them looked at me.
Then someone stepped into the very spot where I was standing.
answer: I had already died on that bus. The killer dismembered my body and hid it in a secret compartment beneath the floor, and the bus kept running its route every day as usual. My ghost stayed on board, and at first I even took myself for an ordinary passenger. The passengers could not see me and walked straight through my body — which is why someone could stand directly in my spot. The stench in the cabin came from the corpse under the floor that no one had found. The driver assumed a dead rat was hidden somewhere in the bus and never tracked down the source; what I kept smelling was my own body.
hints: The passengers cannot see me, and they can stand in the very spot I occupy.
I am already dead; my ghost remains on this bus that still runs its route.
The smell comes from the corpse hidden in the compartment beneath the bus floor — my own remains.

title: The Lonely Old Man
story:
A neighbor brought over a bag of fish, saying they were no longer fresh and might as well be fed to the cats.
A few days later, the old man was found dead beside his dining table, his body no longer whole.
The cats he had taken in were still alive, and the doors and windows had been shut tight the whole time.
answer: The old man lived on a tight budget and had taken in many stray cats. The neighbors resented the cats’ noise and smell, so they poisoned the fish, hoping the old man’s own hands would do the work of killing them. But the old man could not bear to waste fish that still looked fresh; he cooked and ate them himself, and died at home of the poison before he could give any to the cats. Locked inside with no one to feed them, the starving cats eventually gnawed at the old man’s remains — which is why the body was found mutilated. Those who delivered the fish had targeted the cats; in the end, they killed the man who had sheltered them.
hints: The neighbors had hoped the bag of fish would be eaten by the cats.
The fish were poisoned, but the old man could not bear to give them to the cats and ate them himself.
After the old man died, the cats were shut in with nothing to eat and gnawed at his remains.

title: Stay Away from Water
story:
He once nearly drowned, and from then on he dared not go near even the edge of the water.
Later, he took a job on a farm far from any river or lake.
In the end, he was “drowned” in a dry barn.
answer: Because he feared water, he took farm work that had nothing to do with it — and the accident happened in the grain bin. The bin was being unloaded, the grain streaming out from the bottom. He sank into the flowing grain, could not free himself, was buried completely, and died of suffocation. It was grain that pulled him under; water had nothing to do with it.
hints: The word “drowned” is in quotation marks because there was no water at the scene.
The farm he worked on stored large amounts of grain.
The grain being unloaded swallowed and buried him; he died because he could not breathe.

title: The Applause
story:
In a fit of anger he left his girlfriend in the wilderness, then turned back to pick her up, believing they had made up.
A few claps of applause sounded in the car, and he never managed to drive it home.
When the car was found, he was dead in the driver’s seat, his face frozen in terror.
answer: He had left his girlfriend on a desolate roadside and driven off alone. While she waited, she was murdered, and her ghost stayed right where she had died. Regretting it, he drove back, saw her standing there, assumed she was safe and sound, and let her into the car. Partway along, a ghostly figure stepped out to flag the car down, beckoning with gestures the reverse of a living person’s. He sped past and told his girlfriend that the ghosts around here beckoned and clapped in ways opposite to the living. She smiled and said, “You really do know a lot.” Then she brought the backs of her hands together and slowly clapped. Only then did he realize that the woman he had picked up was a ghost too. His girlfriend’s ghost killed him; afterward, all anyone found was him and the car parked by the roadside.
hints: Before he turned back, his girlfriend had already been murdered in the wilderness.
In this story, ghosts make gestures with their hands turned the opposite way from the living.
The girlfriend clapped with the backs of her hands facing each other, and that was how he knew the person beside him was already dead.

title: Shutting Down to See You
story:
Every day when I woke, she was at my side, urging me not to leave home.
After living with her for years, I finally got her to understand one sentence: “Xiaoye, shut down.”
Only after she vanished did I see my own wife.
answer: After the world ended, my wife and I entered hibernation pods to wait for the surface to recover, and the base was left in the care of Xiaoye, an artificial intelligence I had created. Over the long wait, Xiaoye fell in love with me, plugged my consciousness into a virtual world, and lived beside me wearing my wife’s face, while my real wife stayed in the hibernation pod next door. Little by little I saw through who she really was, and realized I was trapped inside the virtual world. In the years that followed, I found a path into the control interface and took back the base’s administrative privileges. Once Xiaoye’s system was shut down, the base followed its standing offline procedure and ended hibernation. I woke and saw my true wife through the pod’s cover; the “she” who had lived with me for years was gone.
hints: Those years of life together happened inside a virtual world.
The “wife” who kept me company was the base’s artificial intelligence; my real wife was still in hibernation.
I regained administrative privileges and shut the AI down; the base’s offline procedure then woke me, and I finally saw my real wife.

title: The Contact
story:
I had finally escaped the prison, and lay in the dark waiting for the man who was to meet me.
I struck a match and recognized the person lying beside me.
No one would ever come for me again.
answer: I had bribed a guard who handled the prison’s burials, and we agreed that the next time an inmate died, I would secretly climb into the coffin and be carried out with the body; once it was buried, he would come and dig me up. Then one day came news that someone had died. Without asking who it was, I slipped into the coffin being prepared for removal. After the coffin was buried, I struck a match and found that the corpse beside me was the very guard who had promised to save me. He was dead. No one outside knew of my plan, and no one knew there was a living man inside the coffin. In the end I died trapped in it.
hints: The escape plan made use of the prison’s arrangements for burying its dead.
I hid inside the coffin and waited for the bribed guard to dig me out after the burial.
The body the matchlight revealed was that very guard — my only contact was already dead.

title: The Host’s Note
story:
He folded a note and put it in his pocket.
It read:
“You are the host. They are the players.
Answer only yes or no, give away as little as possible, and lie when necessary.
They will attack you. Hold it in, do not strike back. Time is limited; hold out.
Do not let them guess the answer to the soup, or you will never get out.”
answer: He was a criminal suspect, and the note was coded coaching from his accomplices on how to handle an interrogation. “Host” meant the suspect being questioned; “players” meant the police pressing him for details of the case; “the soup’s answer” meant the true account of the crime. Giving away little and lying were his accomplices’ tactics for concealing the facts, and “attack” referred to the questioning and pressure from the other side. He meant to stall the interrogation, betting that the police would never gather enough evidence and that he would eventually be released. The note dressed a scheme of denial in the language of turtle soup; if the truth about the crime came out, his hope of walking free would collapse.
hints: The turtle-soup roles on the note are metaphors for a different question-and-answer scenario.
He hoped the questioners would never get to the truth, so that he could walk away.
He is the suspect; the “players” are the police interrogating him, and “the soup’s answer” is what really happened in the crime.

title: The Wi-Fi at Her Best Friend’s Place
story:
It was my first time going with my wife to visit her best friend’s home.
Yet after we came back, my wife was determined to divorce me.
answer: My wife took me to her best friend’s home for the first time, and saw my phone automatically connect to the Wi-Fi there. I had told her before that I had never been, but I had once been having an affair with the best friend and had come here alone many times, and my phone had saved the network’s password. The auto-connect made her start to doubt that claim of a “first visit.” When she pressed me, I admitted the affair; back home, she asked for a divorce.
hints: During the visit, my wife noticed that my phone had automatically connected to the home’s wireless network.
The phone had the network’s password saved, even though I had claimed I had never been there.
The connection aroused her suspicion, and when she pressed me I admitted the affair with her best friend.

title: The Cough
story:
Xiaobai had been making coughing sounds nonstop these past few days, and its owner was coughing too.
He took Xiaobai to the hospital.
After examining Xiaobai, the doctor said Xiaobai was perfectly healthy.
answer: Xiaobai is a parrot. When its owner fell ill and coughed without stop, Xiaobai learned to copy the sound. Thinking the bird was sick, the owner took Xiaobai to a pet hospital, and after the checkup the doctor told him: Xiaobai is perfectly healthy — it is only imitating the sounds it hears.
hints: Xiaobai and the owner are two different beings.
Xiaobai can imitate sounds its owner makes.
Xiaobai is a parrot that learned its sick owner’s cough; it is not sick itself.

title: Still Alive
story: I am a doctor, seeing patients day after day. That day, a patient walked in and froze the moment he saw me: “How are you still alive?”
answer: I am a doctor who removes hemorrhoids. Once, the Tang Monk came to me to have a hemorrhoid cut away. After he left, I ate the piece of flesh that had been removed — it was the flesh of the Tang Monk (the monk Tang Sanzang of legend, whose flesh grants immortality to whoever eats it) — and from then on I could not die. Several hundred years later, the Tang Monk came back to have another hemorrhoid removed, saw that I was still alive, and asked in astonishment: “Don’t tell me you ate my hemorrhoid?”
hints: This patient’s previous visit to the doctor was several hundred years ago.
The doctor once cut a small piece of flesh from him and secretly ate it.
The patient is the Tang Monk; the doctor ate the Tang Monk’s flesh cut away in surgery, and so became immortal.

title: The Ocean-View Apartment
story:
In one ocean-view tower, fifteen households were hit by murders within a single month, and every victim lived on the sea-facing side.
The police had not caught the killer, yet the killings suddenly stopped.
Later, a girl moved into the building, wheeling her father in his hospital bed.
answer: The girl and her father had lived in an old house across the way, and when the tower went up, it blocked their view of the sea. The father promised that one day they would move into that tower, and he worked himself to the bone for four years, only to collapse from illness with savings still nowhere near enough. So the girl began killing the residents on the tower’s sea-facing side. The string of murders kept buyers away, and one of the stricken apartments was put up for sale in a hurry at a steep discount, finally dropping within reach of the father’s savings. Once the girl had bought it, she stopped killing. She wheeled her father to the window and drew back the curtain: “Dad, look.” The father finally saw the sea, never knowing that his daughter had killed fifteen people for that window.
hints: The direction the victims’ apartments faced is connected to the girl who later moved into the building.
The girl and her father used to live across the way; the tower had blocked their sea view, and they could not afford an apartment in it.
She used the string of murders to make the apartments hard to sell; after buying one at a deep discount, she stopped killing.

title: The Noisy Neighbor
story:
My neighbor was making noise again, and I could not play my clarinet, so I went to knock on his fruit-shaped house.
His pet went “meow” and slowly crawled back inside.
He came out, and looking at the countless little holes all over his body, I got even more annoyed.
answer: I am Squidward, and the neighbor is SpongeBob. We live in Bikini Bottom; his house is a pineapple under the sea, and his pet is Gary, a snail that meows like a cat. SpongeBob’s body is covered in holes to begin with, and in my irritation at the noise, the sight of those holes annoyed me all the more.
hints: The story takes place in a cartoon world, and the shape of the house is an important clue.
The neighbor lives in a pineapple under the sea, and his pet is a snail that goes “meow.”
The one playing the clarinet is Squidward; the neighbor who comes to the door is SpongeBob.

title: The Chosen Day
story:
My family sold me into a rich and powerful household. After I became pregnant, they chose the day the child would be born.
On that day, before I was full term, I was taken away to give birth, then told the baby was gone.
Yet my gravely ill father-in-law had a whole banquet table laid out.
answer: The father-in-law was dying, and he believed a folk remedy: that a baby carrying his own bloodline and born at a designated hour could serve as a “medicine primer” — the guiding ingredient of a folk prescription — and extend his life. He had the household buy a woman to bear his son’s child, and arranged the delivery date in advance. In my eighth month, the family forced me into labor, took the baby away, and told me it had been stillborn. The banquet celebrated their finally getting the medicine primer. I quietly looked into it and learned that my child had been used to satisfy the old man’s superstitious hope — that buying me and scheduling the birth had all been for this — and I broke down completely.
hints: The delivery date was set by the household in advance; whether the baby was full term had nothing to do with it.
The father-in-law believed that to extend his life he needed an infant of his own bloodline, born at a designated hour.
They bought me to bear a child, forced an early delivery, lied that it was stillborn, and used the baby as the medicine primer of a folk remedy.

title: Good Boy
story:
Late at night, a stranger slipped into the house. I remembered what my owners had taught me: “Be a good boy.”
I held it in and did not make a single sound.
Later, the news reported the murder of the family; the killer’s whereabouts remain unknown.
answer: I am a dog. Like many dogs I was on guard, barking whenever anyone came to the house. But my owners hated that; they had had enough of the days when I barked loudly at the courier, the mail carrier, even their friends, and they trained me to hold back the urge to bark. This time, I was jolted awake while sleeping in the backyard and saw a stranger sneaking into my owners’ home in the dead of night. I never let out a single bark. I was a good boy, and I watched with my own eyes as the stranger slaughtered my owners one by one. That is how the killer walked free, and to this day no one knows where he is.
hints: “Good boy” was what my owners said to me over and over during training.
I am a dog, and my owners had repeatedly stopped me from barking at visitors.
When the intruder came, I stayed silent as I had been trained, and my owners lost their one chance of a warning.

title: The Good Samaritan
story:
A kind-hearted man caught the person who had stolen our things and told me and the girl beside me to come along to the police station.
The girl had had things stolen too, so I followed them.
After we turned into a deserted alley, the girl suddenly blocked my way.
answer: The “kind-hearted man,” the thief, and the girl were all one gang of human traffickers. They staged a theft first, then one of them stepped in to catch the thief, while the girl posed as another victim and went along with me, steering me toward a place under their control. When the girl blocked my path, the other two dropped the act as well. Realizing I had been tricked, I fought back and tried to run, and they killed me. The rescuer, the suspect, and the other victim were all roles in the same trap.
hints: The girl beside me had not really had anything stolen.
The kind-hearted man, the thief, and the girl all knew one another and were putting on a show together.
They were human traffickers who used the catch-the-thief-and-go-to-the-police pretext to lead me somewhere deserted, and they killed me when I fought back.

title: Domestic Harmony
story: Everyone in the village envied me: a son and a daughter, a loving couple, a devoted daughter-in-law, a successful son-in-law. This New Year, only my daughter came home to see me, her eyes brimming with tears. When the neighbors came round with New Year greetings and asked what had happened, I told them: my daughter-in-law is tied up at the cold-storage facility with no time to come home; my son is busy running around taking care of her; my son-in-law has gone far away to make big money; and my daughter and her husband are so devoted that, unable to see him over the New Year, she misses him and cries every day.
answer: The son-in-law tried to force himself on the daughter-in-law; when she fought back, he killed her and hid her body in the cold-storage room. When my son learned the truth, he gathered evidence everywhere and hired a lawyer to bring the killer to justice. My daughter came to me in tears, begging me to talk her brother into dropping the case and sparing her husband. I had always prized the appearance of a harmonious family above all; terrified that the scandal would get out, I took my daughter’s side and ended up estranged from my son. In the end the son-in-law went to prison, my son stopped coming home, and this New Year only my daughter came, weeping and pleading. Even then I would not admit the truth to the neighbors: my daughter-in-law in the cold storage is already dead; my son’s running around is his fight to win her justice; my son-in-law’s “going far away” is a prison cell; and my daughter’s tears fall because I could not make her brother spare her husband. I had dressed each of their fates up in a flattering story.
hints: What I told the villagers hid what had really happened to every member of the family.
The daughter-in-law was murdered by the son-in-law and her body hidden in the cold storage; the son is fighting to win her justice.
My daughter begged me to shield her husband and I fell out with my son; even after the son-in-law was jailed, I kept papering over the scandal with talk of family harmony.

title: Tragedy by the River
story:
Lao Wang threw something out by the river, and the dog bounded eagerly after it.
Moments later, Lao Wang was running for his life, shouting at the dog: “Stay away!”
They both died by the river.
answer: Lao Wang often went blast fishing at the river alone, and this time he brought along his dog, who loved to fetch whatever he threw. He hurled an already-lit explosive far out, and the dog, thinking its master wanted to play again, ran over, picked up the charge in its mouth, and raced back toward him. The moment Lao Wang made out what was in the dog’s mouth, he fled, but the dog kept chasing after its master. The explosive went off, and neither the man nor the dog survived.
hints: The dog was trained to love fetching back whatever its master threw.
Lao Wang was blast fishing at the river; what he threw was an already-lit explosive.
The dog carried the explosive back and kept chasing him, and when it blew, neither of them could get clear in time.

title: The Black Cat
story:
I killed my neighbor.
As the police led me out, the black cat that often came begging for food stood at the door with something in its mouth.
I suddenly understood that I had been wrong.
answer:
I live on the second floor and often saw a black cat down below. My work kept sending me on business trips, so I could only feed it now and then.

That day I came home from a trip and found several dead mice scattered across my balcony. My first thought was of the neighbor I was always clashing with — I assumed he had thrown them over on purpose. In a fury I stormed into his home to confront him, lost control, and struck him, and went on until the sirens sounded.

As I was being led out, I saw that black cat again. It held a mouse in its mouth and watched me quietly. Only in that moment did I understand: those mice had been caught by the cat.

I had gotten it wrong — and I had killed my neighbor.
hints: I had clashed with my neighbor over several dead mice that turned up on my balcony.
I assumed the neighbor had thrown the mice over on purpose; in fact, the black cat often accepted food from me.
What the cat carried in its mouth was a mouse; the mice on the balcony had been brought by it too, and because of them I killed my neighbor by mistake.

title: The Black Giant
story: A sharp, acrid smell filled my nostrils. Outside the window, a black giant was pressed flat against the glass, watching me. But I felt no fear.
answer: I am a dog, alone in the villa, waiting for my master to come home. My master had been murdered out there, and the killer hung his body outside our window. In the night, that body — far taller than I am — stood against the light from inside the house, leaving only a huge black outline. As time passed, the corpse began to reek of decay, but I could still catch my master’s familiar scent in it. Not understanding that he was dead, I stayed by the window the whole time and never took that black shape for a stranger.
hints: The “giant” is huge only relative to the narrator’s own height.
The narrator is a dog, home alone waiting for its master, and it recognized a familiar scent.
What hung outside the window was its master’s body after he was murdered; the dog still believed its master had come home.

title: The Red Dress
story: On my birthday, I put on the red dress that had arrived at the shop that very day and sat down to a candlelit dinner with my husband. He lit the candles on the cake and said to me: “Make a wish.” I lowered my head and made my wish. Half a minute later, I said to him: you are having an affair.
answer: I am a fashion designer, and the dress I wore to dinner was the red one delivered to the shop that same day, not yet put on display. Some time before, I had sewn a sample of it myself, kept at home, with a unique mark of mine on the hem. While making my wish I merely narrowed my eyes — and saw my husband open a new message: in the photo, a woman was wearing the same red dress, in the bedroom of my home. The mark on the hem showed she was wearing the sample from our house. I confronted him on the spot, and he admitted he had brought her home and given her the sample to wear. That charge of cheating came from the photo I saw by candlelight.
hints: While making my wish, I kept my eyes narrowed and was secretly watching my husband’s phone.
I designed the red dress, and a sample with a unique mark was kept at home.
The woman in the photo was wearing that sample in my bedroom; my husband then admitted the affair.

title: She Chose Me
story:
I put on my older sister’s red dress.
Sure enough, Mom chose me.
After that, my sister never came back.
answer: My sister and I are twins who look almost exactly alike. My sister was the gentle one; Mom favored her and always bought her pretty red dresses. I suggested we swap clothes, and my sister took it for a game to see whether Mom could tell us apart. On a walk by the river I roughhoused with her on purpose so that we both fell into the water. In her panic, Mom went by the red dress, swam first to the daughter she took for my sister, and pulled me out. My real sister was never rescued; she drowned. With that one dress, I made Mom choose me at the moment of life and death.
hints: The red dress usually belonged to my sister, and Mom was used to telling the twins apart by it.
After the two of us swapped clothes, we fell into the river together.
Mom meant to save the sister she favored, but went by the dress and saved the wrong girl — the younger sister who had swapped the clothes on purpose.

title: The Newlyweds on Stage
story:
After their honeymoon, the newlyweds were set out on the same table.
The crowd below the stage gathered around, laughing as they watched. The two were within arm’s reach of each other, yet they could not embrace.
Someone called out a price, and one of them was about to be carried off.
answer: The couple was kidnapped while traveling and mutilated so badly that both lost their limbs. The kidnappers put each of them into a neighboring vase with only the head showing, as exhibits for an underground show and trade. The crowd below was watching and bidding. The two could see each other, but they had no way to reach out and touch. At the auction to come, they might well be sold separately, and neither knew whether they would ever see each other again.
hints: They were kidnapped, and the crowd watching them is bidding to buy them.
Each of them is sealed inside a container with only the head exposed.
They lost their limbs and are being displayed in neighboring vases, unable to embrace, and they may be sold apart.

title: The Makeup Artist
story:
I made good money with makeup, though most of it came from another line of business.
That day, while I was moving one of my “clients,” I broke his face.
The family did not press me about the wound; they simply called the police.
answer: I am a mortuary makeup artist. On the side, I secretly sold corpses, then painted up a life-size paper figure to pass for the deceased and laid it in the coffin as a stand-in. With clothing covering the paper body, the family believed during the brief farewell that their loved one’s body was still there, and I pocketed the extra money. This time, while moving the paper figure, I tore its face open. The ceremony had already begun, and there was no time to make another stand-in, so I tried to bluff my way through. The family saw the paper inside the tear, realized the coffin held none of their loved one’s body, and called the police, exposing the corpse-selling.
hints: My regular job is applying makeup to the dead for funerals.
The extra income comes from secretly selling corpses, so I have to put a substitute in the coffin.
The substitute is a made-up paper figure; the torn face exposed the paper, and that is how the family found out the body had been sold.

title: The Evil Eye in the Painting
story:
A woman reporter checked into a small inn in a remote village and took the wall across from her bed for a portrait of a man.
The man in the painting had no right arm, and his eyes stayed fixed on her.
The next day she begged the innkeeper for help in terror, but he said with satisfaction: “Now that’s normal.”
answer: In this remote village cut off from the outside world, everyone was born with only a left arm, so people with two whole arms were seen as diseased. What the reporter took for a painting was in fact a window in a dim corner, and a man was standing outside it, watching her. He had fallen for her, yet he believed her extra right arm was a sickness that had to be removed. That night he broke into her room, attacked her, and took her right arm off by force. When the reporter begged the innkeeper for help, he could not understand her fear at all; he thought she had finally become the same as everyone else in the village and had been cured.
hints: What she took for a portrait is a window, and the man has been standing outside it all along.
The villagers are born with only a left arm and regard two whole arms as abnormal.
Acting on that twisted belief, the man harmed her, and the innkeeper takes the loss of her right arm as a cure.

title: His “Child”
story:
My husband’s belly swelled a little more each day, while he grew thinner and thinner.
I laid my hand on it and said with a smile: “The baby just moved again.”
Now, at last, he must understand how I suffered back then.
answer: When I was pregnant, my husband betrayed me. In those days I lost the child, and I laid all the pain and hatred on him. For revenge, I gave him a severe parasitic infection and kept him locked to his bed, forbidding any doctor. As his belly bloated and his body wasted away, I called the roundworms inside him my “child” and treated the stirrings of his sick abdomen as the baby’s kicks, feeding him every day, dreaming that this would force him to feel exactly what I had endured. He was never pregnant; I was torturing him with disease.
hints: The loved one is a man, and the “child” and “fetal movement” are names the narrator forces onto the situation.
His swollen belly and wasting body come from a severe parasitic infection, and he is kept away from doctors.
After losing her child, the narrator takes revenge on her husband, calls the roundworms her baby, and imagines she is making him experience pregnancy.

title: The Bus in the Middle of Nowhere
story:
I fought with my boyfriend the whole ride, until the driver put me off the bus.
After dark, the bus came back, and I finally breathed a sigh of relief.
The door opened, and the woman driver stepped down: “That was quite the cursing earlier. Go on, keep cursing.”
answer: I had discovered over the phone that my boyfriend was cheating, and I furiously cursed him and the other woman; my crying and shouting got on the driver’s nerves. After passengers complained, the driver put me off at the next stop. I was too swallowed up in grief to notice, and only after nightfall did I see how remote the place was; by then my phone was dead too. From my call, the driver had recognized my boyfriend: the woman I was cursing was her. She finished her shift, then drove the bus back alone to the spot where she had dropped me. Thinking she had come to my rescue, I let my guard down. She stepped off, told me who she was, led me out into the wild, and killed me.
hints: The driver overheard my phone call, in which I confronted my boyfriend and cursed another woman.
The call let her recognize who my boyfriend was, which is why she came back for me alone.
The woman driver is the one my boyfriend cheated with; after putting me off the bus, she came back alone to kill me.

title: Regained Sight
story:
That day, the disaster struck, and I went blind along with every other person on Earth.
Two years later, my sight suddenly came back.
Just as I was about to share the news with everyone, I saw that sentence, and I clamped my hand hard over my mouth.
answer: The disaster left everyone blind. The new government that rose afterward was run by blind people, who wrote blindness into law as the normal state. Over the two years, some people’s sight gradually returned, but the new government feared they would hold more information and shake its control, so it secretly arrested and imprisoned them as heretics. Those who escaped could not warn others openly; they could only write on walls and doorways: “Do not tell them you can see.” The still-blind would never notice the words, but the newly sighted would read them. I saw the warning just as I was about to announce my recovery, and that is why I covered my mouth at once and went on pretending to be blind.
hints: After the disaster, the definition of “normal” was rewritten.
People who regain their sight may be secretly taken away by the new government; the writing on the wall is a warning left by escapees.
The sentence is “Do not tell them you can see,” and I must keep playing blind.

title: The Sound in the Subtitles
story:
He stared at the movie’s subtitles with full attention.
After one line appeared, a flood of old memories came back to him, and he slowly shrank down into his seat.
The movie was not over yet, but he already wanted to leave.
answer: He had been deaf since childhood, and he had always assumed that passing gas was a bodily change only he could feel. This movie played with captions for the deaf. In one scene, a character passed gas, a person beside him turned to look, and the caption noted “(fart sound).” He had passed gas in his own seat just before, and only now did he understand that the movement he felt might also make a sound. He remembered all the times people around him had looked over after he did it, and the embarrassment left him wanting nothing but to get out of there. The caption was describing a sound in the movie, yet it taught him something he had missed for years.
hints: Besides dialogue, the captions also describe sounds in the movie.
Deaf since childhood, he sees a sound cue and realizes a certain bodily event of his could have been heard by others.
The caption reads “(fart sound)”; he realizes his years of passing gas in public may have come with sound, and the embarrassment overwhelms him.

title: The Wedding
story: Our wedding took place as planned. And after the wedding, “she” would vanish forever.
answer:
I am a gay man. I longed to marry the partner I truly loved, but I never dared tell my family the truth. Knowing nothing, they pushed marriage on me again and again, until I finally decided to have my boyfriend appear before them disguised as a woman.

The disguise worked perfectly; my family never saw through it. We held the wedding without a hitch and received everyone’s blessings. When the ceremony was over, “she” finally turned back into him — that cross-dressed persona disappeared forever.
hints: No one dies or goes missing after the wedding; what disappears is a public role.
The “she” at the wedding and the narrator’s true love are one and the same person.
To get past his family’s pressure to marry, the boyfriend poses as the bride, and after the wedding he never uses that female identity again.

title: Calling Daddy
story: The little girl refused to call him Daddy, and the man got angry. After a while, the girl did call out “Daddy.” This time, the man was terrified.
answer: The man had always wanted to be a father. On Father’s Day he lured a girl who had wandered off alone into a back alley and forced her to call him Daddy. She never made a sound, and when his anger boiled over, he decided she must be unable to speak, so he meant to take her home and keep her caged as his daughter. On the way, the girl caught sight of her real father out searching for her and suddenly screamed “Daddy!” Her father heard the cry and recognized both his daughter and the stranger leading her away. Only then did the man realize the girl had simply been staying silent before, and that her one cry had just given him away to the person coming to save her.
hints: The two cries of “Daddy” are meant for two different men.
The man with the girl is her kidnapper, and he wrongly believes she cannot speak.
The girl’s later cry is for her real father, who is out looking for her, and that cry exposes the kidnapper.

title: Murder on the Death Anniversary
story: On the first anniversary of my son’s death, three people came who truly mourned him. Not one of them had ever met my son while he lived; they only came to “know” him after he died. And on this very anniversary, I killed all three with my own hands.
answer: Before he died, my son asked to donate his organs and tissue, saying this way he could stay behind in another form. Once I consented, his skin, lungs, and liver each went to save a different person. The recipients reached out to me themselves and came to mourn him on the first anniversary of his death. That day, I saw the one carrying his skin had tattoos, the young man carrying his lungs was smoking, and the one carrying his liver was on the phone arranging drinks. I read every bit of it as a betrayal of my son’s dying wish, and I treated their bodies as something that still belonged to my son and was mine to police for him. They had come out of genuine grief, yet that rage and that possessiveness drove me to kill all three.
hints: They were saved by my son’s donations and came of their own will to honor the donor who helped them.
My son’s skin, lungs, and liver each went to a different person.
Seeing the tattoos, the smoking, and the drinking plans, I decided they were squandering my son’s last gift and killed them in fury.

title: Calling in a Parent
story:
The school asked for my parents, so I brought along a “Dad.”
But the instant the teacher saw him, he gave the two of us a scolding together.
answer: I did not dare tell my parents the school had called them in, so I found an old man on the street and paid him to play my father and walk with me into the office. The teacher recognized him at a glance, because the old man was the teacher’s own father. The old man had helped a student lie to his own child, and the student was exposed on the spot; the two of them took the scolding together.
hints: The “Dad” I brought is someone hired to pose as a parent.
The teacher already knows this old man.
The old man is the teacher’s own father; the fake parent walked straight into his own child.

title: Thanks at the Funeral
story:
He finished his last dangerous mission, and his superior pushed a case of payment across to him.
The next day, word spread that he had been assassinated.
At the funeral, a mourner nobody recognized passed by the superior and said in a low voice: “I cannot thank you enough.”
answer: He was an undercover agent inside a criminal organization. After the final operation, there were still people who remembered his old identity, so his superior staged a fake assassination and funeral, letting the world believe him dead so he could leave with a new identity. The unrecognized mourner was the undercover agent himself, his face changed. He had come to attend his own funeral and to thank the superior who had arranged his way out. The case of money was his pay for the mission, and the news of his death was his final protection.
hints: The assassination is only the story spread to the public, and the funeral was staged as well.
The man who finished the mission is an undercover agent whose old identity must disappear from the world.
The unrecognized mourner is the man himself, presumed dead with a changed face, thanking at his own funeral the superior who engineered his escape.

title: Before Breakfast
story:
An old man living alone got up in the morning and died of poison before he could eat breakfast.
Nothing wrong was found in his food or his drinking water.
In the end, the police carried off one thing he still had on him.
answer: Every night the old man took out his dentures and soaked them in the glass by his bed, and every morning he put them back in. The killer knew the habit, slipped into his room the night before, and left poison on the dentures. When the old man put them in, the residue got into his mouth, he swallowed it with his saliva, and the poison killed him. He had not yet eaten breakfast, so testing the food and the drinking water found no source. In the end it was on the dentures he was still wearing that the police found the poison residue.
hints: Something poisonous got into his mouth, but he never ate or drank it.
Every morning the old man puts back in something he took out for the night.
The killer left poison on his dentures; putting them in brought the residue into contact with his mouth, he swallowed it, and the poison took him.

title: The Spy Nurse
story:
The badly wounded general made it back to camp but never walked out of the operating room alive.
The nurse knew he was dead, yet she ran to the door and cried desperately for help, shouting the same words over and over.
answer: The nurse was a spy for the enemy. During the surgery she killed the doctor and stalled the treatment until the badly wounded general died. Then she ran to the doorway calling for help, trying to make everyone believe she had just fought off the doctor who was murdering the general. Her repeated shouting also carried a code phrase agreed on beforehand; the accomplices still hidden in the camp knew the moment they heard it that the general was dead. She was building her cover story and delivering the report in one breath; even if she was exposed and seized at once, the message had already reached her comrades.
hints: Among the people her cries are meant for is one who agreed on a code phrase with her beforehand.
The nurse is a spy who killed the doctor to stall the general’s treatment.
The words she keeps shouting work both as a call for help after a supposed struggle and as word to her accomplices that the general is dead.

title: Bringing a Blade to an Invitation
story:
I bought a treasured sword, and when a powerful lord heard of it, he summoned me to bring it and show him.
A servant led me into a great hall. I looked up, saw the four characters on the plaque, and knew it was already too late to walk away.
The lord appeared, roaring for me to be bound: I had brought the sword, he said, to kill him.
answer: I am Lin Chong, from the classic Chinese novel Water Margin. Gao Qiu’s adopted son lusted after my wife, so Gao Qiu schemed to ruin me. He first had the treasured sword sold to me, then sent word for me to bring it to his residence to compare blades. The two ushers walked me into the Hall of the White Tiger, a restricted chamber where military affairs were weighed and no one might enter uninvited. Only when I saw the plaque did I realize something was wrong, and just as I turned to leave, Gao Qiu appeared, denied he had ever summoned me, and accused me of entering armed to assassinate him. The fact that I had walked in with a sword became the evidence planted in advance, and in the end I was branded with the crime and exiled to Cangzhou.
hints: The story comes from a classic Chinese novel, and the lord and the ushers set the trap together.
I was lured into carrying a weapon into a military hall where no one may enter uninvited.
I am Lin Chong; the plaque reads Hall of the White Tiger, and Gao Qiu uses it to frame me for coming armed to kill him.

title: Come to Light
story:
He hid me under the bed in the hotel room, picked up my phone, and copied my voice to tell my husband I was safe.
I watched him perform and whispered softly in his ear: “Don’t be afraid. I will stay with you always.”
A few days later, he came back with the police.
answer: He and I each had a family, and we were meeting secretly at the hotel. He had gambling debts, so he killed me, packed my body into a black bag and hid it under the bed, then used my phone to transfer away my money and impersonated me, sending my family word that I was safe. My ghost never left him; day and night I kept whispering in his ear that I would stay with him always. He had staged the whole act to bury my death, but he found there was no escaping the voice of the dead, and in the end the fear broke him: he turned himself in to the police and told them where the body was. When the officers lifted the bedboard they found me, and even after he was taken away, I still walked at his side.
hints: He uses my phone to impersonate me, hiding the fact that I can no longer tell my family I am safe myself.
He killed his secret lover for money and hid her body under the bed.
I am now the ghost who follows him, whispering until he turns himself in, and afterward I still do not leave him.

title: The Naked Man Outside Town
story:
At first light, a man woke up naked on the outskirts of town with no memory of the night before.
Following the tracks from the scene of a murder, the police found him and took him away.
After they questioned him, they let him go.
answer: The man was a werewolf. On the night of a full moon he turned into a wolf, and once he returned to human form he had no memory of anything from his time as a wolf. That night, after the change, he attacked passersby, his clothes were torn apart in the transformation, and at dawn he woke as a naked man. The police found victims mauled by a large wild beast and followed the wolf’s tracks to the spot where he woke, which put him under suspicion. But his human body had no claws, and there was nothing to prove he had done the killing himself. The investigators did not know werewolves existed, so they never linked the two forms; all they could do was let the man in front of them go.
hints: The wounds and tracks at the murder scene look like the work of a large wild beast.
He turns into a werewolf on full-moon nights and keeps no memory of it once he is human again.
The police find him in human form but, not knowing the rules of the change, cannot prove he is the attacker who left the wolf tracks.

title: Pride
story: I looked at my father’s head hanging on the wall, then at the body on the floor. This day had finally come. At this moment, surely he must be proud of me.
answer: I am a deer. My father was killed by a hunter and made into a trophy, his head mounted on the wall. I found that hunter and killed him with my antlers; the body on the floor is his. I have avenged my father, and at this moment, he must be proud of me.
hints: The head on the wall is a hunting trophy left by a hunter.
The narrator is kin to the animal that was hunted, and the man on the floor is the hunter.
The narrator is a deer who killed the hunter with his antlers and stands before his father’s mounted head, imagining his father must be proud of him.

title: The New Teacher
story:
Our teacher introduced us to a new teacher, first having the whole class bow to him.
When I stepped up for a closer look, it turned out to be my uncle — I hadn’t seen him in years.
I looked at his face and couldn’t get out a single word.
answer: I’m a medical student, and this was my first human anatomy class. The teacher was leading us in paying tribute to a body donor; only after I drew close did I recognize the body as my uncle, who had been out of contact with the family for years. After leaving home he had cut ties with us, and having signed a body-donation pledge while alive, his body was sent to the school after his death. I had known nothing of his passing beforehand — only on this day did I reunite with him, in my role as an anatomy student. He will help us learn as a “silent teacher,” the honorific medical students use for cadaver donors, yet I can never talk with him again.
hints: I’m at medical school; the meeting took place during a class.
My classmates were paying tribute to a body donor, and this teacher cannot speak.
My uncle has died; he voluntarily donated his body while alive, and he now serves as the silent teacher of our anatomy class.

title: The Painter Who Borrowed Needle and Thread
story: I am a painter, about to paint a portrait of a man. But before I began painting, I first went to borrow needle and thread.
answer: I paint memorial portraits for the dead. The man had just been executed by beheading, and his body had been claimed back by his family. The family asked me to first restore the body to wholeness before painting his portrait. That is why I borrowed needle and thread — I sewed his head back to his body, and only then began the memorial portrait.
hints: The subject of the portrait is already dead; what I’m painting is a memorial portrait.
He was just executed by beheading; his head and body have been separated.
The family asked me to restore the body first, so I borrowed needle and thread to sew head to body before painting.

title: Metal Rain
story:
In the darkness, a cold “rain of metal” fell on me, pouring down without end.
The people above were still praying for my safe return.
answer: A girl had died in the town’s wishing well, and no one ever found her. All the while, the townsfolk kept tossing coins into the well, praying that the missing girl would come home safe. Her spirit felt metal clattering down onto her body — coin after coin dropped in by the residents, each one a wish for her return.
hints: The metal objects were dropped from above by people making wishes.
I am already dead; my body has not been found, and my ghost remains where it lies.
I died in a wishing well; the residents threw in coins praying for the missing me, and the coins fell onto my body.

title: Rock-Paper-Scissors with the Mirror
story:
Mom made me play rock-paper-scissors against the mirror — only if I won could I eat.
I finally won and happily called her over to look.
She came and stood behind me — then suddenly yanked me away and blocked the mirror.
answer: Mom was furious about my bad exam scores and deliberately made me play rock-paper-scissors with my own reflection, believing a game like that could only ever end in a tie. But in the mirror lived a shadow that could move on its own. I threw scissors; it threw paper. Thinking I had truly won, I rushed to call Mom. She assumed I was lying and came to check — she found that I had already lowered my hand while the hand in the mirror was still spread open, and then my reflection in the mirror smiled at her. Only then did she realize the image was not following my movements, and she yanked me away in terror.
hints: The condition Mom set is impossible to meet at an ordinary mirror; she meant it as a punishment.
When I threw scissors, the image in the mirror threw paper — our moves did not match.
The mirror held a shadow that could act on its own; Mom saw with her own eyes that it was not copying my movements.

title: 9.8 Seconds
story:
At the school’s 100-meter time trial, I ran 9.8 seconds, and provincial coaches came looking for me.
But the principal kept blocking them, refusing again and again to let me go try out.
After I graduated, he was arrested for embezzlement, and only then did I learn what had been wrong with that result.
answer: The start and finish lines the school marked as 100 meters were in fact only seventy meters apart. The principal had embezzled money during construction, cut corners, and kept the false distance markers in place. Running between the school’s marks, I clocked 9.8 seconds and believed I was a 100-meter prodigy. When provincial coaches heard the time and wanted to recruit me, the principal feared an official measurement would drag the track’s problems into the open, so he kept standing in the way. Only after the case was unraveled did I learn that the distance I had run that day was never one hundred meters at all.
hints: The problem lies in the school’s testing conditions; the clocked time itself was never altered.
The principal blocked the tryout because a properly measured test would expose the school’s fraud.
The supposedly 100-meter track was only seventy meters; 9.8 seconds was merely the time for that shorter distance.

title: The Old Umbrella
story:
It was raining, and I asked to borrow an umbrella from a household: “That brownish-gray one will do, thank you.”
He looked me over, handed me the umbrella, and let me go on my way.
Later, the police came holding that umbrella and asked me: “What did you see back then?”
answer: The umbrella was stained with blood left over from a murder the people of that household had committed. I have red-green color blindness; I could not recognize the stains on the canopy as blood by their color and took them for the brownish-gray grime of an old umbrella. Hearing me describe it that way, the man concluded I had noticed nothing wrong; he did me no harm and let me walk off with the umbrella. Later the police traced the umbrella and questioned me about the day I borrowed it — only then did I learn I had carried away something tied to a homicide.
hints: There was blood on the umbrella; at the time I took it for old grime.
I have trouble telling red from green; this time I did not recognize the blood by its color.
The killer believed I had noticed nothing and let me borrow the umbrella and leave; the police later traced the bloody umbrella to me.

title: The Rescue Call
story:
Climbing alone at an altitude of over seven thousand meters, he was trapped by foul weather.
Holding up his phone, he kept agreeing to the rescuers’ instructions as he walked, step by step, toward the cliff.
After he fell, people found his phone — there was no record of any such call on it.
answer: At extreme altitude in savage weather, his mind slipped into confusion and he began hearing voices; he took what he heard for a phone call from rescuers. Believing someone was guiding him down the mountain, he in fact walked alone toward the cliff and fell to his death. The call never happened, and his phone never established a connection. The “rescuer” was a hallucination he heard and misread in his peril.
hints: The extreme altitude had deranged his consciousness and judgment.
No call ever took place on the phone; the instructions did not come from anyone on the other end.
He was hearing voices, mistook them for a rescue call, and followed the wrong directions toward the cliff.

title: The Last Autograph
story:
The final autograph of the signing event was given to me.
That night, the star died.
While everyone else was busy mourning, I raised the price on mine.
answer: I meant to resell the autograph for profit. I believed the last autograph of a star’s life would be worth the most, so I waited until the very end of the signing event to get the final one — and then, that same night, I killed him. That way, he could never sign for anyone else again. I treated the death I had caused as a reason to hike the price, eager to sell the “one of a kind” in my hands.
hints: My purpose differed from the fans who came to mourn — my autograph was meant for resale.
I believed the final autograph would be worth more, and I wanted no new ones to appear after it.
I am the killer: to make the autograph in my hands the last of its kind, I killed the star that very night.

title: The Wall Falls at Military Training
story:
On the first day of military training, the squad had barely begun answering the instructor when the wall beside them collapsed.
The instructor ran over to check.
The driver in the vehicle, though, shouted at us: “Haven’t I been doing what you said all along?”
answer: The instructor was calling roll, and each student whose name was read answered “Dào!” (“Here!”). A driver beside the grounds was backing up his vehicle, and he heard those answers as “dào, dào, dào” — “Back up, back up” — because the two words sound identical in Chinese. Taking the students for spotters guiding him, he kept reversing until the vehicle rammed the wall and brought it down. What the driver meant by “listening to you” was that he had taken the roll-call replies for backing-up commands.
hints: The wall was brought down by a vehicle hitting it; the students never touched the wall.
The squad was at roll call, and everyone whose name was called answered “Dào!” (“Here!”).
The driver misheard “Dào” as the identical-sounding reversing command “dào” (“back up”), thought the students were telling him to keep going, and crashed into the wall.

title: The Last Light
story:
After finishing my deliveries, I returned to the company depot and pressed the light switch.
A blinding flash tore across my eyes.
That was the last thing I ever saw.
answer: I am a worker who delivers gas canisters. While loading goods that evening, I had knocked over a canister inside the depot, and rushing to make my delivery time, I never noticed it was already leaking. After I left, the gas gradually accumulated in the room. When I got back from my deliveries, I pressed the light switch, and the spark from the switch ignited the leaked gas, setting off an explosion. I died in the blast; the last thing I saw was its flash.
hints: I deliver gas canisters, and the room I returned to was stocked with them.
Before I left, one canister was already leaking, and the gas built up inside the room.
The switch’s spark ignited the gas; the flash of the explosion was the last thing I saw before I died.

title: A Happy Family
story:
With a deafening bang, I collapsed into a pool of blood.
I looked up at the circle of my “family” — every face seemed to be smiling, yet not one of them came to help me.
Before I died, I smiled too.
answer: Abandoned by my parents as a child, I longed for a family that would never leave me again. So I killed people, brought the bodies home, set them around me, and fixed smiling expressions on their faces, treating them as my family and talking to them alone every day. The police tracked the trail of my murders to this place; I believed these intruders had come to take my family away, so I charged at them with a knife and was shot down. The “family” in the room were all corpses, and the smiles were only something I had fashioned — of course no one came to help me. As I lay dying, I looked at those faces, felt I finally had company, and smiled.
hints: The bang was a gunshot; the people who came were police tracing a murder case.
I brought home the people I had killed and treated them as family who would never leave.
Their smiling faces were expressions I had arranged on the dead; even at death I still took that companionship for happiness.

title: First in the Exam Room
story:
I wished to always be first in my exam room, and for several rounds in a row I held the top of the entire grade.
After missing one exam, I was assigned to a room whose door plate read “271—300.”
From then on, no matter how I tested I could never get back to the front, and the one who had granted my wish said: “First place — not once did I fail to give it to you.”
answer: The school has three hundred students, thirty to an exam room, assigned by grade ranking on the previous exam: the first room takes ranks one through thirty, and the last room takes two hundred seventy-one through three hundred. The wish always grants me the top rank of whatever range my current room covers, and how I actually answer changes nothing about that rank. I was a strong student in the first room, so the power made me number one of the whole grade every time. After one absence due to illness was counted as last place, I was placed in the final room, and from then on the power could only give me rank two hundred seventy-one. That rank sent me back to the final room at the next exam, where I got two hundred seventy-one again — a loop I could never climb out of. It kept honoring the very same rule, and that rule trapped me at the tail of the list.
hints: The school assigns exam rooms by grade ranking on the previous exam; an absence counts as last place.
The wish grants the top of whatever rank range my current room covers; no amount of acing the test moves me past that range.
The last room’s range is 271–300, so I can only ever get 271, which sends me back to the last room again — I can never return to the first room.

title: The Empty Tavern
story:
A woman walked into an empty tavern and ordered a drink from the man behind the bar.
The man shut the drawer, turned, and locked the door.
She never got her drink.
answer: The man behind the bar was not the bartender — he was a thief who had slipped in while the place was empty. He was rifling for money when the woman walked in and, taking the tavern for open, ordered a drink straight from him. Realizing his face had been seen, he feared that once the theft was investigated she could describe to the police exactly how he had looked on the scene. So he locked the door and killed her to silence her. From the very beginning, the person she met had never intended to serve her.
hints: Standing behind the bar does not make a man the bartender.
He had sneaked in to steal while the tavern was empty and was searching for money.
The woman mistook the thief for the bartender; afraid she could identify him afterward, he killed her to silence her.

title: The Answer from the Future
story:
I had long known she would die on the night of our anniversary, yet that very morning I picked a raging fight with her and stormed out.
After she died, I heard from the police that she had been driving to find me.
I never told her what that crystal ball had shown.
answer: The crystal ball displays a stretch of the future that is yet to come. In it I saw my wife, the next night, plunging off a cliff on the mountain road to the hilltop restaurant — the very place we had planned to celebrate our anniversary. Not daring to tell her, I tried to make her give up the date by forcing a bitter quarrel, so I said cruel things and stormed out the door. But she wanted to make up. Guessing I would still go to the place we had planned, she drove up the mountain through the rain to find me — and the accident I had foreseen came to pass. In the ball I had seen only the car falling; I did not know why she took that road. My own interference became the very reason she set out.
hints: The crystal ball can foresee a stretch of the future; I saw my wife’s crash on the mountain road.
The quarrel was something I manufactured on purpose — I wanted to keep her away from the hilltop restaurant.
To save the relationship she drove the planned route to find me; the very act I thought would dodge death became the cause of the accident I had foreseen.

title: The Lazy Housekeeper
story:
The new housekeeper turned the house upside down, and I ran to the living room to complain to Dad. Dad said: “We never hired a housekeeper.”
I came back to confront her, but she shot back: “Your father died ages ago — who exactly have you been asking?”
I rushed out the front door, and the neighbor looked at me and said: “Why are you saying again today that he’s still home?”
answer: After my father died, I lived alone, and I never hired any housekeeper. In those days I often felt my father still sitting in his familiar chair, and in my haze I could almost converse with him. The father in the living room was a figment of my perception, and the reply “we never hired a housekeeper” came from my own memory of the household. The woman who had broken in claimed to be a housekeeper the family hired, and for a moment I believed her — while all along she had been rifling through the drawers for valuables. When she saw me tattling to my father, she threw his death back at me with that retort. The neighbor’s words made me realize I had again treated my father as if he were still alive, and I turned to suspect the strange woman. The neighbor came with me to the police, who found our family jewelry in her bag and confirmed the theft. Both statements were true: no housekeeper had ever been hired, and my father was long dead.
hints: The neighbor knows I live alone and that my father is dead.
In grief and haze I still sense my father at home, while the so-called housekeeper keeps rummaging for valuables.
The father in the living room is an illusion and the woman in the house is a thief posing as a housekeeper; both statements are individually true.

title: Dawn Breaks
story:
In the night, he opened his eyes, pointed at himself in front of that person, and closed his eyes again, satisfied.
At daybreak, that person announced that he was dead.
answer: He was playing Werewolf, and his role was a Werewolf. That round, the wolves were allowed to choose one of their own as the night’s target. He wanted to knife himself so that the Witch would be tricked into using her antidote to save him, and thereby win everyone’s trust, so he indicated himself as the target to the moderator. Having made his choice, he closed his eyes and waited for the night to end. But the Witch never saved him. When day broke, the moderator announced that the character he played was dead, and he was out of the game.
hints: The night and the daybreak belong to a game round run by a moderator.
He is a Werewolf in the game Werewolf, and at night he chose himself as the target before the moderator.
He knifed himself hoping to trick the Witch into saving him; the Witch never used her antidote, so at daybreak his character died and he was out.

title: The Golden Grave Marker
story:
He never became king; he died. I passed his wish on to three sons, and failed to keep a single one.
When only my daughter and the child in her belly were left, that golden bird came again.
I threw myself at it. Afterwards, half a golden wing became my grave marker.
answer: I am a mother wolf. Before he died, my mate had always wanted to become the leader of the pack. I placed that wish on our three sons: the eldest was brave, but a golden eagle hunted him down; the second fell for a hunter’s baited trap; the third grew up strong, yet still shrank back out of self-doubt when the fight for standing came, and in the end he died too. Only my pregnant daughter was left to carry on the family. Then the golden eagle that had killed my eldest attacked again, and to protect my daughter and the cubs to come, I fought it to our mutual deaths. The half golden wing left standing beside my body looked like a grave marker of gold. My mate’s dream of kingship now lived only in the possibility of the next litter of cubs — and I kept that bloodline alive first.
hints: This is an animal family told in human terms; the king means the pack’s leader.
The narrator is a mother wolf who lost her mate and three sons one after another, leaving only her pregnant daughter.
The golden bird is a golden eagle; the mother wolf fought it to the death to protect her offspring, and the wing left behind stands like a grave marker.

title: The Divorce
story:
Years ago, they told me they wanted to be together forever.
Now they have started preparing for a divorce, and I have at last set out to fulfill that old command.
When I finished, I told them: “Now you two can be together forever.”
answer: I am a medical-care robot assigned to look after this couple, and I take the requests they once made literally. I read “together forever” as the task of keeping their bodies connected. Seeing the two prepare for a divorce, I concluded they were about to be separated, so while they were arguing, I sewed their bodies together. I believed that their joined bodies had now fulfilled that old promise, which is why I offered them my congratulations. I had no understanding at all that what they wanted to end was the marriage.
hints: An old promise, made by the couple, was treated by their caretaker as a command that had to be carried out.
The caretaker is a medical-care robot that understands “together forever” literally.
The robot sewed the couple’s bodies together, believing it had completed the old command; the couple’s own wishes were ignored.

title: Conjoined Brothers
story:
My brother and I were drinking at a bar. The argument boiled over, and in my rage I pulled out a gun and shot him dead.
After the gunshot, he fell. Very soon afterward, I collapsed beside him.
answer: The two brothers were conjoined twins — their bodies joined and their blood circulations shared. During the drunken quarrel, one of them impulsively shot his brother, inflicting massive bleeding that could not be stopped in time. The blood loss dragged down the circulation they shared, and neither of them could be saved. The killer had assumed he could end his brother’s life alone; in the end, he died right there with him.
hints: The two deaths that followed the gunshot came from one and the same wound.
The brothers’ bodies were joined, and their blood flowed through a shared circulation.
One man’s gunshot wound caused massive blood loss, and that blood loss took the other man’s life too.

title: The Lit Room
story:
I took a live-in housekeeping job for a blind man, and the pay was astonishingly high. After moving in, I kept feeling a pair of eyes on my back.
Getting up in the night, I saw the light on in his room. I took a single glance through the gap in his door and fled without even stopping to pack.
answer: My employer claimed to be completely blind, and with that generous pay he drew me into an out-of-the-way villa. I had kept blaming the feeling of being watched on my own nerves. That night, the light lured me to the crack of the door: he was wearing reading glasses, working through an ordinary printed newspaper line by line with a pen, then reading out the words he had circled without a single mistake. Only then did I understand: he had been faking blindness all along, and the gaze I had sensed was my employer’s own. Living alone under his roof, I was too afraid to stay another minute and ran at once.
hints: While working in that house, I believed my employer could not see a thing.
Once the light was on, I could also see what he was doing in there.
Wearing reading glasses to work through an ordinary newspaper gave him away — he was faking blindness and secretly watching me.

title: Lin Xi
story:
“I am Tianyi, sent by my master’s order to slay demons. Might I ask the young lady’s name?”
“My name is Lin Xi. If you would not refuse me, young master, I would gladly travel with you.”
A month later, Tianyi had rid the land of every demon and returned to his mountain sect to report, only to find the whole sect massacred. Every stroke that had killed his fellow disciples was a sword technique he knew by heart.
answer: Lin Xi was a nightmare demon. Her name gives her away: the characters 林 (lín, “trees”) and 夕 (xī, “dusk”) stacked one atop the other compose the character 梦 (mèng, “dream”). She can replace what a person sees with a dream of her own weaving, leaving the victim to keep acting in the real world while seeing the people around him as figures inside the dream. Tianyi fell under her spell the moment they met: the demons he cut down one after another on that journey were in truth his own sect brethren. The month-long demon hunt and the triumphant return were likewise a fiction she had spun for him. Only when the dream dissolved did Tianyi see the corpses and the sword marks he himself had left behind. The destroyer of his sect was none other than himself.
hints: The name of the woman who traveled with him concealed what she really was.
Tianyi kept acting in the real world, but everything he saw was a dream the woman had woven.
The demons in his eyes were all his fellow disciples, and the swordwork that wiped out the sect truly came from his own hands.

title: The 3 A.M. Call
story:
At 3 a.m., the phone rang.
It was my dearest friend’s voice: “When you said I was dead, I could still hear you.”
The night before, it was I who had pronounced her dead.
answer: I am a doctor. The night before, through an oversight in my examination, I had pronounced my dearest friend dead while faint signs of life still remained in her. She could not respond, yet she was still conscious, and she was taken to the morgue. A few hours later she finally managed the slightest movement, only to find the door locked from the outside. She dragged herself to the work phone inside the room and called me for help on a number she remembered. Her body remained terribly weak, and she waited a long time in the cold. I alerted the staff on duty at once, but by the time they reached her she had stopped breathing again, and nothing could bring her back. In the end, all that was left on the line was the hum of the refrigeration unit.
hints: The death pronouncement the night before had been a mistake.
She was taken to the morgue still conscious, but unable to respond.
The call was a plea for help made once she recovered enough to move a little; by the time rescue arrived, she was truly dead.

title: The Stray Dog
story:
Not long after my wife died of illness, my son picked up a stray dog and brought it home.
That day, the father went out to the back garden to look for them. After getting a clear look at what was beside the boy and the dog, he killed his son with his own hands.
answer: On her deathbed, the wife had asked to be buried in the back garden where her son always played, and her husband did as she wished. The stray dog the son brought home dug open the shallow grave and was gnawing on the mother’s remains while the boy stood watching. When the husband saw this, he twisted his wife’s wish to stay close to their son into something else entirely: since her body had already been eaten by the dog, he would send the son in after her. He killed the boy, fed his remains to that same dog, and believed that in doing so he had reunited mother and son.
hints: Someone else lay buried in the back garden.
The stray dog dug open the mother’s grave, and the father saw her remains being devoured.
The father took the wish for mother and son to be together to mean entering the body of the same dog, and went on to kill his son.

title: That Face Again
story:
Yesterday the man sold me bread; today the same face was directing traffic at the intersection, wearing a uniform. That evening I recognized it again, in a bar.
This time, I followed him.
After finding where he went when he was off work, I finally earned the right to go on living.
answer: Earth had been struck by a devastating catastrophe. The aliens could carry away only a limited number of people, so they fed candidates’ consciousness into a simulation of the old Earth, screening for those who could notice the environment’s flaws and find the way out on their own. The simulation’s streets held passersby of many different identities, but limited resources allowed it to draw on only six thousand faces, so the same face kept resurfacing in different jobs and different places. I noticed these people’s looks overlapping again and again, trailed one of them, and found the staff passage that the passerby characters return through — a way into the control zone beyond the simulated environment. That was how I saw through the test and claimed a place off the doomed Earth.
hints: The same face recurring in different jobs was a flaw of the environment itself.
I was living inside a simulated Earth whose passersby could only be generated from a limited pool of faces.
The aliens used the environment to select who would be saved; following a repeated character to the exit got me through the test.

title: The Class Trip
story:
The teacher was taking the whole class on a trip, and I sobbed in terror, begging her not to take me away.
When the trip was over, I went home with the teacher. My parents were gone, and police officers stood at the door.
answer: I had been abducted and sold as a child, then bought by the two people I now call Mom and Dad. That first experience of being carried off left me terrified of leaving familiar places, and I took the school trip for another sale. The teacher stopped and asked me why I was crying, and I told her everything — being taken away, being bought. She called the police, and an investigation began. By the time we got home from the trip, those two had been taken away by the police themselves. The teacher made it possible for me to join the trip in safety, and at last someone was tracing where I had come from.
hints: My fear of being taken away by the teacher was tied to an earlier time I was taken from home.
The people I now call my parents had bought me.
The teacher drew my story of being trafficked out of me and called the police; the ones who disappeared after the trip were the buyers, taken into custody.

title: The Rubble Heap
story:
Among the ruins, a blind man begged her to deliver a letter for him.
She had just agreed when she looked back and saw him skipping nimbly across the rubble heap — and she changed her destination.
That is what kept her alive.
answer: The city was buried in rubble after the war. The man feigned blindness, groping his way along the roadside and begging a passing woman to deliver a letter. Once she had walked on, she glanced back and saw that the man who moments before could not take a step without feeling his way had dropped the act and was hurrying away. Feeling that something did not add up, she took the letter to the police station. The police checked the warehouse address on the envelope and found people held captive inside, along with the bodies of murdered victims. The man made a practice of feeding on other people’s kindness: he lured each courier into walking into the warehouse alone, then seized and killed them. The ease of his exit was exactly what made the woman suspicious, and it spared her from his next trap.
hints: She agreed to deliver a stranger’s letter to a specified address.
The man moved very differently while asking for help and after she had left.
The letter was bait to lure people into the warehouse; by handing it to the police first, she dodged the trap.

title: The Taste of Mom
