The brother is waiting inside. By the time I see the iron chain, I am already the next one they mean to lock up.
hints: The age the student gave has nothing to do with the woman’s actual age.
She has been in that house for four years, and she cannot leave freely.
The student is an adult disguised as a small child who lures teachers into home visits and kidnaps them together with his brother.

title: Back to Camp
story:
The expedition leader told him to turn back, and he said, “I’m not going back without the summit.”
He truly stood on the summit, and he survived the blizzard too.
At daybreak, he finally made it back to the familiar camp.
Later, people found his body there.
answer: Close to the summit, the climbing team ran into foul weather and the leader ordered a retreat. He insisted on pressing on, reached the top alone, and was then caught by the blizzard. Out of contact with the team all night, he barely made it through to daybreak on the mountain, by then drained of nearly everything. Unable to keep waiting in such weather, the team took him for dead, packed up the supplies, and pulled out of the high camp. With his last strength he dragged himself back to camp, only to find no one there and none of the gear that could have restored him and kept him warm. He could not go on down the mountain, and he froze to death in the very place he had counted on for rescue.
hints: What he found was the camp his team had once occupied.
After striking out alone, he lost contact with the team for the whole night.
Believing him dead, the team withdrew with the people and the supplies; by the time he reached camp, he had no strength left to descend.

title: His Skin
story:
I watched him every day.
One day, he said goodbye to everyone and said he would never come back.
I put on his skin.
Tomorrow, people will still see him.
answer: He was a virtual streamer who appeared on screen as a digital character. He announced his graduation — a permanent end to streaming as that character. I was one of his viewers, and I could not accept letting the character vanish, so I took up his virtual character model and went on streaming as that character myself. The “skin” is the model an operator wears in a stream; the person inside it in the new streams is me. The original streamer has retired.
hints: He used to appear on screen in the form of a character.
What I put on can swap a person’s appearance in a livestream.
He is a retired virtual streamer; I keep playing the same character in his model.

title: She Likes Me
story:
She hardly ever spoke in class, yet she stared at me every single day.
More and more, I came to believe she liked me.
Sometimes our eyes met, and her mouth would open and close; I couldn’t hear a sound.
Not once did she smile.
answer: She can see the ghosts that cling to people, and she knows to scatter them by silently reciting an incantation. Ever since she was little, talking about the things she saw got her treated as a freak by her classmates, so she went quiet. Lately a ghost had fastened itself onto me, and all she could do was keep her eyes on where it hung, mouthing the incantation to drive it off. The movement of her lips is the chant; her gaze toward me is her watching the ghost attached to me. I mistook this unbroken act of rescue for affection.
hints: Her lips were repeating a string of words that actually had an effect.
She could see something clinging to me that I could not see.
She was silently chanting an exorcism; I mistook her constant watching for affection.

title: Footsteps on the Stairs
story:
The screaming downstairs stopped.
One, two, three… nine.
I tried to get out through the balcony, bracing on the armrests to push myself up.
But my body gave only a twitch.
Ten, eleven… seventeen.
The sound drew closer and closer.
answer: Not long before, I had been in a car accident. My legs no longer move, and for now I live in a wheelchair. A killing happened downstairs, and from the top of the stairwell I saw the man with the knife — and he saw me. Then he started up the stairs toward me. I swung my wheelchair toward the balcony and, in blind panic, tried by old habit to stand and get over the railing, but my body would not perform the motion. With my old ways of escaping — running, jumping — gone, I froze in terror and could only listen as the killer’s footsteps crossed the stairs one by one, nearer and nearer. Those numbers were me counting his steps.
hints: The numbers track the movements of someone drawing closer.
I had just been in a car accident, and my body could no longer move the way it used to.
I sat in a wheelchair as the killer came up the stairs; in panic I tried to stand and flee, and found my legs would not move.

title: The Candy Lure
story:
The little girl would not stop crying.
A strange man took out some candy and reached a hand toward her, meaning to take her home with him.
She shook her head, backing away and crying for her mother.
He failed to take her away. Afterward, she never cried again.
answer: After the zombie virus broke out, the zombies nearby home in on sound. The man came across the little girl crying all alone and wanted to take her back to his own safe shelter, but he was afraid that explaining out loud would only raise the danger. So he brought out the candy, hoping to calm her first, quiet her down, and then lead her away. The girl was wary of strangers; she refused the candy and kept crying for her mother. The crying had already drawn the zombies. The man could not get her clear in time, and the girl was killed by them.
hints: There was a danger in that area drawn to sound.
The man wanted to bring the girl to a safe shelter.
Zombies came for her crying; his attempt to quiet her with candy and lead her away failed, and he could not save her.

title: A Narrow Escape
story:
I had taken off my jewelry and my keys, but the metal detector kept going off.
I missed my flight and went back to the hospital.
The second time I was discharged, I felt relieved instead.
answer: I had just had abdominal surgery abroad and was flying home. At the security check, even after I took off every piece of metal I carried, the alarm kept centering on my abdomen. Remembering the discomfort that had lingered ever since the operation, I decided to go to a hospital first, and so I missed the flight. The imaging found that a metal surgical clamp had been left inside me during the earlier operation. The hospital operated again and took it out. I was simply relieved that the security check had alerted me, and that this dangerous oversight had been caught and dealt with in time.
hints: The metal setting off the alarm could not be removed from clothing or luggage.
I had had abdominal surgery not long before.
A surgical clamp the doctors left inside me set off the alarm; only on re-examination was it taken out.

title: Taking Its Place
story:
After my little sister died, I picked up a habit.
Once, she caught me, and all she said was, “You destroyed it — so take its place, and stay.”
I stayed there ten years, and for the first time I felt I had a home.
After I lost her, the old method stopped working.
I bought needle and thread, sewed myself a layer of skin, and crouched in a stranger’s yard, waiting.
When the owners came home, they screamed and called the police.
answer: My sister and I were orphans with no home. She was bitten to death by a house’s guard dog while foraging for food, and I killed that dog; from then on I would often slip into other people’s houses to kill their dogs. Once, the woman of the house caught me, found that I had already killed her pet, and shut me up in her home to take the dead animal’s place. In those years of being kept like a pet, I took the life of being fed and allowed to stay for the warmth of a home. Ten years later she died, and I had nowhere left to belong. I tried going back to killing dogs, hoping to meet another person willing to keep me, but it never worked again. So I killed another family’s dog, sewed its skin into a coat and put it on myself, and crouched in their yard waiting — hoping the owners would take me in as the replacement pet. What that owner saw was their dog dead and a person in dog skin barking at them, and they called the police in terror.
hints: My habit began when my sister was bitten to death by a guard dog.
The owner who first caught me made me take the place of her dead pet.
Kept like a pet, I took it for a home; later I killed dogs and wore dog skin to find a new owner, and was taken for a dangerous intruder.

title: The Woman Who Jumped
story:
She had lived in the dead city for a long time, believing she was the last living person.
The moment she leapt from the high-rise, the phone in her pocket rang.
She regretted it, but there was no time to answer.
answer: The zombie virus broke out, and the people around her turned one after another. She hid alone in the city for a very long time, with no answer coming back from anyone, until she believed herself the only living human left; in the end she jumped from the building in despair. While she was falling, a call came in from someone still alive. The ring made her realize, all at once, that she might still be able to reach other survivors, that the loneliness might not go on forever. Hope of living welled up in her — but the decision of a moment ago could no longer be taken back, and she died.
hints: A zombie disaster had struck the city she lived in.
She never confirmed the whole world was empty — she simply went unanswered for a very long time.
Another survivor called; by the time she realized she might still have companions, it was already too late.

title: Dad in the Vent
story:
I can see with only one eye.
While I was showering, a familiar face appeared in a crack in the ceiling.
“Dad, what are you doing up there?”
I recoiled in fright and slipped.
From then on, I could never see him again.
answer: My father had already been murdered by a killer. His body was hidden in the space above the bathroom ceiling, his face turned toward the vent. Showering, I looked up and saw his face and his open eyes, thought he was hiding up there watching me, and slipped as I recoiled in fright. One of my eyes had been blind to begin with; in the fall, my one seeing eye was badly pierced by a hook on the wall, and in time I lost that sight as well. My father could not answer because he was long dead; I can never see him again because I have gone completely blind myself.
hints: The face in the vent could not respond to my words.
When I slipped, my one seeing eye was injured.
My father’s body was hidden above; startled, I slipped and destroyed the last eye that could see.

title: Spitting Out the Pills
story:
Every day, my wife’s voice urges me to take my medicine.
I answer her, and once she goes quiet, I secretly spit the pills out.
Back in the days when I took my medicine faithfully, I would go days at a stretch without seeing her.
answer: My wife died in a car crash. Unable to accept losing her, I began to see her and hear her speak — hallucinations that went on and on. Under the doctor’s treatment, the hallucinations gradually faded: I saw my wife less and less, heard her voice less and less. I knew the medicine was doing it, but I took her fading for one more parting, and so I began secretly spitting out the pills, wanting to keep feeling her there beside me. The wife in the hallucinations kept her old caring ways, and still urged me every day to take my medicine on time.
hints: No one else can see or hear the wife I speak of.
The doctor’s treatment was gradually fading my hallucinations.
My wife died long ago; to keep her hallucination, I secretly stopped taking my pills.

title: Ghosts Outside
story:
I woke in a strange cabin, my head pounding.
Scattered on the floor were sheets of paper, each reading, “Don’t go out. There are ghosts outside.”
The door was unlocked.
Beside a pool of blood lay one more note in the same handwriting: “I was wrong. Run.”
answer: An obsessive stalker of mine drugged me and carried me to an abandoned cabin at the edge of the woods. She knew I was afraid of ghosts, so she left the warnings on purpose: she wanted me too frightened to step out alone, so I would settle into the life together she had arranged. What she did not know when she picked the house was that a serial killer was using its basement to store his victims. Coming back, the killer found her and me lying unconscious, and attacked her. Wounded, she understood at last that the true danger was inside the house. With her remaining strength she wrote “I was wrong. Run,” and then he killed her and dragged her body down into the basement. When I woke, the door was still unlocked. The first warnings that had kept me inside were her lie; the last note was the warning to flee that she left as she died.
hints: Both notes were written by the same person — but what she knew had changed between them.
The first warnings were meant to keep me, who feared ghosts, inside the house.
My captor was attacked by the killer hiding in the house; dying, she wrote “Run” and retracted her invented haunting.

title: The Perfect Statement
story:
After he was brought into the police station, he volunteered that he had a major case to confess to.
He talked all afternoon, never stopping his reminders: “Write that sentence down too — don’t leave anything out.”
When he finally got the written statement to check over, he nodded with satisfaction.
The officer slammed his pen down onto the desk.
answer: He is a crime novelist who got brought in for drunken trouble. He lied that he had taken part in a complicated crime and had the police record his so-called confession — in truth, he was dictating the novel he had only just plotted. The officers wrote out the names, the places, the course of every action, and handed it to him to check. He read it through, nodded in satisfaction, and even admitted outright: “I made every word of it up — perfect that you’ve organized it into a manuscript for me.” Only after a whole afternoon’s work did they see that the detailed document in front of them was a story he had spun under the cover of a confession, and that is why they were furious.
hints: The details he told were complete, yet they matched no real case.
He normally earns his living writing stories; his insistence on word-for-word record had another purpose.
He passed off the crime novel he had plotted as a confession, had the police take it down for him, then admitted it himself.

title: The Perfect Surgery
story:
I am a plastic surgeon. That operation was the most satisfying one I have ever performed.
She recovered beautifully, and left with a smile: “From here on, leave the money to me.”
In the end, I never saw a cent of it.
I dared not say who she was, and in the end I killed myself.
answer: I had run up enormous gambling debts, and I meant to exploit the identity of a wealthy woman client. She looked strikingly like my wife. I killed the client, took her ID and her bank credentials, and operated on my wife to make her look still more like the woman, so that my wife could pass as the client and withdraw a large sum of money. My wife went through with the surgery, but once the money was in her hands she left on her own, leaving me behind with the debts. I dared not expose her impersonation to the police, because that would drag my own murder into the light. I had meant for the surgery and my wife to carry me out of the hole; instead my accomplice abandoned me, and I killed myself between the debts and the dread of my crime coming out.
hints: The person on the operating table was my wife; together we were copying another woman’s identity.
The wealthy woman being copied — I had already murdered her.
My wife took the money under a false name and left; I got nothing and dared not expose our conspiracy.

title: The Perfect Machine
story:
We are descendants of the ones who fled the Earth, come back to search for the legendary “perfect machine.”
A pack of hairless dogs ran through the streets.
I raised my gun at one of them, and it lunged and sank its teeth into me.
When my turn came to come out of the machine, I too could only go on all fours.
The pack of “dogs” suddenly looked familiar.
answer: The old machine on Earth was first built to remake human bodies and erase the flaws it judged in them. Later it stopped accepting anyone’s refusal and enforced modification by its own standard of performance: to lighten the burden of an upright body, it rebuilt people onto four legs, reshaped their limbs, and stretched out their lives. The first wave of people fled the Earth; their descendants — us — knew only that a machine that could better the human body had been left behind, nothing of what its remaking finally became. Coming back with the expedition, I met people who had lived for decades after modification, took them for hairless dogs, and my raised gun drew their attack. In the course of searching, we found the modification center still running, and I was put through it as well. When I came out no longer able to stand upright, I finally understood: those creatures were all people the machine had rebuilt to its standard.
hints: The machine is directly tied to the appearance of those creatures.
It was our ancestors who fled the Earth; we never knew the full outcome of the modifications.
The machine rebuilt human bodies onto four legs and lengthened their lives; the hairless “dogs” were the people who stayed — and I had been remade the same way.

title: Hello, Uncle Wang
story:
Ever since I was old enough to remember, I had never met my father. Mother said he had been abroad all this time.
Years later, he suddenly came home, and I got a form of address wrong.
That very day, of my two parents only he was still alive.
And yet I could not go home with him either.
answer: Father had worked abroad for years, and Mother had fallen into an affair with our neighbor Uncle Wang. Uncle Wang came by so often that I had grown used to opening the door for him, knowing he was going upstairs to see Mother. The day Father suddenly returned, I failed to recognize the man I had not seen in all those years and blurted out: “Hello, Uncle Wang — Mother is upstairs waiting for you.” Questioning me further, Father pieced together the affair between his wife and the neighbor, and in a rage he killed them both; he was then arrested by the police. I had lost my mother, and my one surviving parent was locked away, so I had to be taken in and raised by someone else.
hints: I mistook my father for the other man who kept coming to see Mother.
The form of address I got wrong exposed Mother’s relationship with the neighbor.
Father killed Mother and the neighbor and was arrested; with my only surviving parent in custody, there was no one left for me to go home to.

title: Online Shopping
story:
He did not like dumplings, yet for days the shopping app kept recommending frozen dumplings and a whole pile of dumpling-making supplies.
He handed the phone to his wife: “Surely it got the recommendations wrong this time?”
She looked at the screen, smiled, and said: “Quite fitting.”
Before long, he was dead.
answer: The couple shared one shopping account, and every browsing record shaped the recommendations that account received. The wife had long resented his endless squandering of money and his refusal to lift a finger around the house, and she had formed a plan to kill him and turn his remains into filling for dumplings. Again and again she browsed dumplings and related supplies on the shared account, and those visits changed the recommendations her husband saw as well. He assumed the app was only guessing at his own tastes, never suspecting that what surfaced there was his wife’s preparation. She later carried out the murder, and in the end he was killed.
hints: The browsing records of two people feed into the same account.
The wife had been looking at dumplings and related supplies for some time.
The wife planned to kill him and make dumplings from his remains; her browsing shaped the recommendations he saw.

title: My Mother Won
story:
Father was dead set against my being with her, but Mother said: “Go ahead. It’s fine.”
On his sickbed, Father told me a secret. Crying, I went to ask Mother, and she told me another one.
Father died later on, and yet at last I smiled.
answer: She was the younger sister my family had adopted, and after we grew up we fell in love. Father opposed it; Mother supported us. When Father was terminally ill, he told me that my sister was in fact his illegitimate daughter, believing this would make me understand that we were brother and sister by the same father. I went to ask Mother, and only then learned that I was actually the child of Mother and another man — something Father had never known. The two of us had different birth fathers, and Mother had known this all along, so the blood relation Father feared did not exist. Father was furious when he learned of Mother’s concealment, and he later died of his illness. I smiled because I finally understood that my beloved and I shared no blood relation, and the relationship could go on.
hints: The reason for Father’s opposition was tied to a secret about who she really was.
Mother knew who the other one’s birth father was, holding a fact Father did not know.
She was Father’s illegitimate daughter, while I was Mother’s child by another man; we shared none of the blood relation Father believed we had.

title: Past Saving
story:
He pushed the car up to a house and stopped.
He counted his money, sighed, and said: “That’s the end of me.”
The person beside him smiled and held out a hand.
answer: They were playing a Monopoly-style property board game. What he pushed was a toy car serving as his game piece, and the house was a model standing on his opponent’s land. His move landed him on an estate where the opponent had already built houses, so he owed rent. His cash and whatever he could raise from his assets were no longer enough to pay, and he had no choice but to declare bankruptcy and bow out. The opponent held out his hand because he was waiting for the in-game money to be settled.
hints: The car and the house are sized nothing like everyday transport or housing.
He and the person beside him were taking turns playing a game.
He moved his car piece onto the opponent’s property, could not pay the rent, and went bankrupt in the board game.

title: No One Stopped Me
story:
I set a ladder against the outside wall, climbed in through the window, and carried out a case of jewels.
Several police officers watched the whole time.
When I got back to the ground, a woman took the case with tears in her eyes, thanking me over and over.
answer: I was a firefighter taking part in the rescue after a fire. The blaze in that house had been brought under control and the residents evacuated, but the fire-damaged stairway was temporarily impassable. The owner asked us to help retrieve a case of jewels left upstairs; once we confirmed that route was usable, I set up the ladder, went in through the window, and returned the case to her hands. The police officers at the scene were there for security; they knew I was helping the resident recover her belongings, so they simply watched and kept the work space clear.
hints: The woman was the homeowner, and she knew exactly what I was carrying.
The house’s normal entrance was unusable; I was helping with a rescue.
I was a firefighter; after the fire, at the owner’s request, I set up a ladder and retrieved the jewel case she had left upstairs.

title: The Silent Ritual
story:
My parents had been arguing constantly of late. Mother asked me on the sly how to make a bank transfer, and she often waved her hands about at home without a word.
After dinner, Father went out, and she slipped out right after him.
I followed her quietly to the square.
Dozens of people were making the same movements she was, yet not a trace of music could be heard anywhere around.
answer: Mother had recently joined a neighborhood square-dancing troupe. Father suspected her frequent outings meant she was seeing someone, and the two of them fought over it; to keep the peace, she practiced and went out while avoiding him. The transfer she asked about was payment to the troupe leader for the team’s matching uniforms. Waving her hands at home was dance practice. To spare the surrounding residents, the troupe all wore headphones to hear the music, so to outsiders it looked like a crowd moving in unison with no audible accompaniment. Only by following her did I come to see that all these seemingly secret doings revolved around one and the same dance activity.
hints: The transfer paid for something a whole group would use together.
The movements she practiced at home were ones she also did with the others.
She had joined a headphone-wearing square-dance troupe and paid for the uniforms; the headphones kept the music from being heard by others.

title: The Midnight Train
story:
Five minutes before midnight, the man boarded the train and studied the passengers one by one.
“You’re twenty-eight this year?” “That’s right.”
“You’re fifty-five?” “That’s right.”
Then he asked an old lady: “Sixty-nine?”
“That’s right. Once it’s past twelve, I’ll be seventy.”
The man’s face went white.
answer: The man could see the age, in whole years, at which each person would ultimately die — a number that steps up at midnight on every birthday — though he could not see his own. He noticed that the death-ages shown for the passengers in this carriage were identical to their current ages, so he went from one to the next, asking to verify. For the earlier passengers, death might fall on any day within their current year of age, so the timing could not yet be pinned down. But the old lady said she would turn seventy in five more minutes, and what he saw was that she would die at sixty-nine. That meant she would not live to reach this birthday of hers. Add the fact that many others around him were likewise in the final year of their lives, and the man strongly suspected the train was about to suffer a deadly accident. He could not know whether he himself would die — and he was already standing in the carriage he believed doom was about to reach.
hints: The ages he sees and the passengers’ actual ages are not the same kind of information.
He sees the age at death in whole years, and the old lady is about to pass beyond that age.
The old lady will die at sixty-nine yet turns seventy in five minutes; he realizes she will not live to see midnight.

title: The Birthday Curse
story:
A man calling himself a sorcerer said my child would die on his birthday.
I rushed off to beg someone to break the curse. After hearing me out, that man smiled and said: “He’s a fraud. There’s no such thing as a curse.”
I was finally at ease.
On the birthday, the child died all the same.
answer: The so-called sorcerer was a charlatan who played at the mystic arts, and he had frightened us with the threat that the child would die on his birthday. A local who knew the man saw through the trick and told us there was no real curse, and because of that we let our guard down. When the fraud learned he had been exposed, he broke into our home on the birthday itself and killed the child with his own hands, so that others would believe his prophecies came true. The judgment that there was no curse was correct — the death came from the very man who had voiced the threat carrying out a murder.
hints: What was said about there being no curse was true.
The person who issued the threat could still take the actions of an ordinary man.
To make his prophecy come true, the fraud broke in on the birthday and killed the child himself.

title: Blood by the Cradle
story:
The man came home. With one stroke of a sword he killed the dog he had raised for years.
The next moment, he was overcome with regret.
answer: Coming home, he found his dog covered in blood and raced frantically into the nursery: the cradle had been knocked over, blood dripped down from it, and the baby was nowhere to be seen. In his fury the man cut the dog down with a single stroke of his sword — but as the dog let out its last whimper, a baby’s cry rang out. Only then did he find the infant lying safe beneath the crib, with a wolf’s corpse beside it. The dog had fought the wolf to protect the baby, which was why it was covered in blood; now it had died wrongly accused.
hints: The man connected the blood on the dog with the baby’s disappearance.
There was another animal in the house, and the dog had fought it.
The dog killed the wolf that broke in, and the baby was unharmed beneath the crib; the man had wrongly taken the dog for the one who hurt his child.

title: The Magnet
story:
I touched my toy to my teacher’s gold bracelet. She froze, and then wept with anger.
She stormed into the principal’s office, and the argument went on for a long while.
At home I told my father, and he gave me just one warning: “From now on, when you play with that, keep away from your mother.”
answer: What I was playing with was a magnet. My teacher wore a bracelet the principal had given her — the two of them were married, and he had told her it was pure gold. My magnet clung to the bracelet unmistakably, exposing it as an iron core plated with gold. The teacher realized her husband had deceived her and went to his office to fight it out. The moment Father heard my story, he remembered that he too had once given Mother gilded jewelry passed off as pure gold; afraid my playing with the magnet at home would expose that, he told me to keep away from her.
hints: My toy can attract one very common metal.
The teacher had always believed the bracelet was solid gold, a gift from her husband.
The magnet clung to the iron-cored, gold-plated bracelet and exposed the principal; Father had given Mother the same kind of fake gold jewelry.

title: Lucky in the Crowd
story:
The chandelier came down and I was unharmed, but the waiter’s arm was covered in blood.
Fire swept past my side and set a lady’s dress alight.
I finally stood before my enemy without a single wound on me.
Overhead, a beam cracked open once more. I cried out: “I dissolve the contract.”
This time, the pain fell on me.
answer: Five years ago, the banquet host’s factory polluted the river and killed my little sister. For tonight’s revenge I had bought a disaster-warding contract: whenever anyone stood near me, any harm that should have befallen me would be transferred to the people around me; I could dissolve it with a spoken word, but upon dissolving it I would bear, in equal measure, all the harm previously transferred away. The contract took effect tonight. I had believed it would shield me and carry me to my enemy, and when I signed I gave little weight to the price bystanders would pay. Disasters struck the banquet one after another; I passed through the chandelier, the flames, and the rest untouched, while innocent guests were hurt in my stead. Amid the shaking of the earthquake, that protection carried me to my enemy; when I saw the decorative beam split open overhead once again, I could no longer bear to let others keep suffering disaster in my place. I dissolved the contract of my own will; the harm already transferred came back onto me, the protection ceased, and I was badly injured beneath the falling debris.
hints: My walking away unharmed and the injuries of those around me are in direct exchange.
The contract passes disasters meant for me on to the people beside me.
After I dissolved the contract, the harm transferred earlier came back onto me; I gave up a revenge that had been bought with other people’s suffering.

title: My Favorite Author
story:
I gave my favorite horror novelist a birthday present: a fountain pen.
His assistant carried the gift home ahead of him; he himself was still at the venue.
I went home, opened up my screen, and waited for him to get home too.
The moment he walked in the door, I dialed the police.
answer: I was obsessed with the writer and wanted to peep into his life, so I gave him a fountain pen with a hidden camera inside as a birthday gift. The assistant carried the gift back to the writer’s study, and at home I waited on the feed for him to return. On the screen there was a bound person. Once the writer walked in, he began tormenting that person, and the setup and the acts matched, in uncanny detail, a killing from one of the novels I had read. In horror I realized he might be feeding real crimes into his fiction, and I called the police at once. The police later found the victim and supporting evidence, confirming that the crime matching the novel had indeed been committed by the writer.
hints: The pen I gave away lets me see the writer’s study from my own home.
What happened in that study resembled a crime from one of his novels.
Peeping through the camera in the pen, I watched the writer torment a bound person and discovered his fiction was drawn from real crimes.

title: Rain
story:
It rains here every day, yet at night there are always “stars,” clear as can be.
I took one look through a telescope.
A point of light closed, then opened again.
It had been watching me the whole time.
answer: After I died, I was confined in an underworld space built to imitate the streets and daily life of the human world. The dead here are penned and raised by demons as food. The points of light overhead come from the demons’ eyes, which look like a sky full of stars from afar; they gaze down on the dead being farmed below, their eyes closing and shifting. The rain that falls day and night without pause is their drool, dripping endlessly at the sight of food. Through the telescope I made out the eyes clearly — and the mouths beneath them, and the falling liquid — and at last I understood what kind of place I was living in.
hints: I am already dead; life here only imitates the human world.
The points of light that look like stars belong to creatures that are watching me.
Demons farm the dead from above; their eyes are the stars, and their drool is the rain that falls every day.

title: Better to Remember Than to Meet
story:
The doctor said: “I’m sorry. I did all I could.”
I wanted to see my husband one last time, but he held down the white sheet: “Don’t look. Remember him as he was.”
I did not listen.
That freshly stitched wound had no business being on his body.
answer: My husband had been in a coma since a car crash, kept alive by machines. His attending physician was involved in the illegal organ trade; he falsified records of deterioration and death, killed my husband, and harvested his organs. Telling me he had done all he could and trying to stop me from viewing the body were his way of hiding the new surgical wounds. I insisted on lifting the sheet and saw sutured wounds across the chest and abdomen that matched nothing in his recent treatment schedule. The wounds alone could only make me suspect an operation I had never been told about. I called the police afterward, and only after investigating the records and the transactions did they confirm that the death was tied to organ harvesting.
hints: The doctor kept me from the body to hide something recently done to it.
Nothing in the husband’s recent treatment schedule accounted for that wound.
The doctor faked the decline and the death to harvest organs illegally; the fresh sutures betrayed the undisclosed surgery.

title: The Perfume
story:
She lost her parents as a child, and not long after, her little brother died too.
On her birthday, her boyfriend handed her a small bottle of perfume.
She took one clear look at the bottle and, before he could even open it, turned and ran.
answer: After their parents died in a car crash, she and her little brother once found a small bottle filled with liquid. She took it for a wish potion and coaxed her brother along, telling him that if he drank it, Mom and Dad might come back. He believed her — and died from swallowing the toxic industrial liquid inside the bottle. She never forgot the moment she made him drink it. Years later, the perfume bottle closely resembled that little bottle in shape and cap. The sight of it brought her brother’s death and her own words rushing back, and she fled in terror.
hints: She had not smelled the perfume yet; it was the look of the bottle that struck her.
In her childhood there was a small bottle of liquid tied to her brother’s death.
She had fed her brother poison believing it a wish potion; the similar perfume bottle brought the memory surging back.

title: Craving a Bowl of Soup
story:
In the famine, I caught the smell of meat broth — the first in far too long.
Seeing me rush in, the owner of the house asked only one question: “Are you alone?”
I nodded and begged him for a bowl.
I never made it back out that door. The next day, the smell of meat broth drifted from the place again.
answer: The great famine was at its height, yet from a house not far off drifted a rich meat-broth smell the likes of which no one had known in ages. Half dead with hunger, I burst in to seize food — and saw a smile on the owner’s face that made my skin crawl. He had been using the broth to draw in starving people like me, people who came rushing in for food, and then killing them to make new bait. What simmered in the next pot was me.
hints: In this famine, the owner somehow keeps replenishing his supply of meat.
The people who come begging for soup are the source of that supply.
He kills the starving drawn in by the broth and stews their bodies into the next pot; I became one of them.

title: A New Big Brother
story:
The boy said: “Mom, I want a big brother to play with me every day.”
The woman’s face changed: “But… you already have one.”
He thought for a moment, then said with a smile: “Then swap him for a new one.”
answer: The boy had grown into a teenager. Deprived of family company all his life, he had turned to kidnapping to build the family he wanted. He was holding a woman and an older boy captive, forcing them to play mother and big brother. The woman knew that the moment they failed to satisfy him, he would kill them and go looking for replacements. The current “brother” was still locked up in another room, yet the boy, finding his company not enough, asked for a brother again. The woman, afraid this meant he would kill the one he had, hurried to remind him that he already had a brother. That line — “swap him for a new one” — confirmed he meant to keep satisfying himself by replacing his family members.
hints: What the woman feared was what he would do once he had made his request.
She and the so-called brother were both being held in that home to play their roles.
The boy kidnapped people to play family and killed them when they displeased him; asking to swap the brother meant the current one was about to die.

title: He Vanished
story:
His eyes fell off, his nose kept growing smaller, and his arms broke too.
I picked his eyes up off the ground and tucked them into my pocket.
answer: He was a snowman I had built. I used buttons for his eyes, and shaped the nose and the arms out of snow as well. As the weather warmed, the snow gradually melted: the buttons lost their support and dropped off, the snow nose shrank, and the arms collapsed and broke. I put the button eyes away safely; the snowman went on melting afterward until he finally disappeared.
hints: These changes have to do with temperature.
His eyes could be picked up and kept because they were small objects added when he was made.
He was a snowman; the button eyes fell off, and the snow nose and arms melted away.

title: After Spring Came
story:
After winter set in, he walked into a half-built high-rise at a shut-down construction site and never came back.
When work resumed in spring, the workers found his body.
His head bore a severe wound, yet nothing that could have caused it could be found anywhere around him.
answer: In winter, icicles formed along the eaves of the towers on this northern construction site. As he passed below, one icicle broke loose, struck his head, and killed him. The site stayed shut down, so no one found him in time. Months later the weather warmed, the icicle had long since melted, and his body was finally discovered by the workers returning to the site. That is why the wound was still visible, while the object that had struck him was gone.
hints: Several months passed between his death and the discovery of his body.
The object that caused the injury disappears as the weather turns warm.
An icicle fell from high above in winter and killed him; by spring it had melted away.

title: The Last Square
story:
The first piece landed on top of me, and I stayed where I was.
The second piece landed beside me.
This time, I disappeared together with all my companions in the same row.
answer: I was one small square already settled on the screen in a game of Tetris. A new piece stacked on top of me, but my row still had a gap, so the condition for clearing it was not met. Then another piece landed beside me and filled the last empty space in the row. The game promptly cleared the entire line, and I vanished from the screen along with every other square in it.
hints: The falling pieces and I belong to the same geometric grid of a screen.
When a horizontal row is filled completely, it is cleared away as a whole.
I am one small square in a game of Tetris; the last empty spot beside me was filled, and the whole row vanished.

title: One Good Night
story:
The man died in his own home. The windows were closed, and the knob on the inside of the door lock had been turned to locked. The smart speaker in the entryway gave its last response: “Good night. The door is locked.”
Yet the man’s phone had already dialed a call for help before that.
answer:
The man had let an acquaintance into his home. After committing the murder, the guest left, pulling the door shut behind him. The windows had been closed all along, and the door showed no sign of forced entry.
The man had once connected the electric knob on the inside of his door lock to the entryway speaker, setting it up so that saying “good night” would lock the door. The killer knew about this habit. After stepping out, he woke the speaker from the other side of the door and said “good night.” The speaker received the command and drove the indoor knob to lock the door.
The knob really did turn from the inside, but that only proves the locking device was indoors. The call the man dialed while dying, together with the speaker’s logs, set the police asking who had spoken that “good night.”
hints: The knob really did turn from the inside, but a device can drive it.
The speaker can hear someone speaking at the door, and the man had set up one bedtime phrase as a command.
After the killer left, he made the speaker carry out the locking from outside the door.

title: Little One Is Here
story:
Waking from my afternoon nap, I heard a voice from the living room: “Mom, Little One is here.”
I lived alone. That very afternoon, I moved out.
On my first night in the new home, I could not sleep. At midnight, the same words came from the living room again.
I touched my flat, empty belly and sent a message to my former landlord: “I want to move back.”
answer:
I had lost the child in my womb. After leaving the hospital, I lived alone with a parrot for company. The landlord was a small man who often called himself “Little One.” I rarely spoke with him, and I had never once said the words “Mom, Little One is here” in front of the parrot.
That day, waking from my nap, I heard the parrot suddenly say the sentence. Suspicious, I looked into it and found that the landlord had repeatedly let himself into my home late at night. Pressed by my questions, he admitted he had slipped sleeping pills into my drinks; once I was deep asleep, he would climb into my bedding, hold me, and call me Mom. That sentence was something he had said to me.
Terrified, I moved out at once, and the parrot came with me. In the new home I lay awake all night, and when I heard the parrot imitating him again, I found myself missing the feeling of someone nestled close to me. Thinking of the child I had lost, I decided to make “Little One” my child, so I contacted the landlord about moving back.
hints: Both times, the voice was the same parrot’s, and it moved to the new home with me.
The sentence was one the parrot learned from the person who kept sneaking into my home.
I moved out because I feared the landlord; by the time I wanted to move back, I had decided to let him stay by my side in a different role.

title: Pastries and a Gunshot
story:
Little Red Riding Hood carried a basket of pastries to visit her grandmother.
The wolf arrived ahead of her, and the hunter followed along.
After the gunshot, Little Red Riding Hood helped her grandmother up and fed the pastries into her mouth.
Watching this scene, the wolf lying on the ground finally closed his eyes.
answer:
This is a fairy-tale world where wolves can talk and live among people. The grandmother had once saved the wolf from a hunter’s chase, and he had watched over her in secret ever since.
Little Red Riding Hood’s mother wanted the inheritance all to herself and had poisoned the pastries. Little Red Riding Hood knew this and set out with the basket anyway. The wolf had overheard the two of them planning through the window, so he reached the grandmother’s house first, hoping to get the old woman away from them.
The grandmother was frail and could not walk. The wolf settled her by the bed and stood guard at her side. When Little Red Riding Hood came in, the wolf blocked her way and tried to snatch the basket from her. At that moment the hunter, who had trailed her all the way, burst in, took the wolf for an attacker, and shot him.
The hunter pulled the fallen wolf aside, and Little Red Riding Hood went to her grandmother and fed her the poisoned pastries. The wolf had protected the grandmother for years, yet in the end a rescue that looked so timely destroyed her last chance.
hints: This is a fairy-tale world; the wolf understands human speech and can protect people.
The wolf knew the pastries were wrong and tried to stop Little Red Riding Hood from handing them to her grandmother.
The hunter misread the danger: his gun helped Little Red Riding Hood carry out the mother’s and daughter’s plan.

title: The Thief’s Warehouse
story:
I had been a thief all my life, and I did not stop even in old age.
When my children came home from a long trip, they knew the moment they walked in that I had been out stealing again these past few days.
The next day, the warehouse where I hid my loot was emptied out, yet many new things had appeared in the house.
answer:
In my old age my memory grew more and more muddled. I kept mistaking my own home for a place to burgle, while the old habits stayed with me: stealing things and hiding them in the warehouse.
While the children were away, I found the house empty and “stole” our own belongings piece by piece, carrying them off to the warehouse. The children came home to a nearly empty house and understood at once what had happened.
They knew where the warehouse was. The next day they moved the furniture and household goods back home and put everything in its place. When I next went to the warehouse and found it empty, I assumed someone had stolen my loot; back at the house, I discovered it full of “new things.”
hints: The children know where I hide my takings, and this time they also knew where those things had come from.
My habit of stealing is still with me; my memory of our own belongings is what has failed.
The things in the warehouse had been in our home all along, and the children moved them back.

title: The Smile
story:
Mom and Dad had not sat together like this for years.
Shoulder to shoulder, hands linked, just like when I was little.
I put away my needle and thread, stood in front of the sofa, and finally smiled.
Neither of them ever scolded me again.
answer:
When I was little, my parents were devoted to each other and loved me dearly. I loved sewing and often made clothes for my dolls, and they always praised how skillful I was.
Then they both lost their jobs, and the family grew poorer and poorer. They quarreled constantly and took their resentment out on me. I was grown by then, but I still longed for them to go back to the way they used to be.
After one quarrel, I killed my parents. I arranged their bodies on the sofa, then used needle and thread to fix their clothes and their linked hands in place, posing them in the intimate posture I remembered.
I put away the needle and thread and watched my parents sitting quietly together. I took the scene before me for a return to the beloved days of my childhood, and a contented smile came over my face.
hints: Besides making clothes, the needle and thread were used to hold the posture in place.
My parents sit quietly on the sofa, no longer able to answer me.
I killed my parents, then posed their bodies into the loving shapes from my childhood memories.

title: The Secret in the Shoes
story:
Every time I ordered food delivery, I asked for two pairs of chopsticks. The pair of men’s shoes by the door always stood neatly in place.
Then one day a text arrived from a number I did not know: “He’s dead.”
Before I could even reply, the bedroom door opened.
answer:
I lived alone. To make strangers believe there was also a man in the home, I kept a pair of men’s shoes at the door and noted “two pairs of chopsticks” on every delivery order.
A week earlier, I had quarreled with a deliveryman over a lost package, and he held a grudge. Suspecting the shoes were just for show, he quietly slipped a few grains of rice inside them and came back later to check. The shoes had not moved, and the rice was still there.
Combined with what he had observed of me during that time, he concluded that I had been pretending to live with a man, and he decided to break in and take revenge. The text saying “He’s dead” came from him too: the man I had invented to protect myself had, in his eyes, been exposed.
By the time he sent that text, he was already inside my home. Soon after I received the message, he pushed open the bedroom door.
hints: The “he” in the text never actually lived in that home.
Someone tampered with the shoes by the door, using them to test whether anyone else lived there.
The two pairs of chopsticks and the men’s shoes were camouflage for my living alone; the sender of the text had already slipped inside.

title: The New Dress
story:
A woman left work wearing a one-of-a-kind dress.
That night, she died on her way home.
The dress was immaculate. Someone had carefully spread out its skirt, smoothing every pleat at the waist.
answer:
The woman was a mortician. While preparing a body, she fell for the dress the deceased was wearing, secretly swapped it off the corpse, and wore it home from work.
The dress’s designer was obsessively protective of her work’s form. She had once had her lover wear the dress, but could not bear how it deformed whenever the lover walked. In the end she killed her lover, tidied the dress, and kept the body as a motionless display mannequin.
Later the designer discovered the dress had been swapped away. She tracked down the mortician and followed her as she left work. In the designer’s eyes, the walking woman had once again ruined her carefully arranged work. She killed the woman, posed the body and skirt anew, and smoothed out the pleats.
The body was replaced with another, and the dress was restored exactly as she demanded.
hints: The woman’s work brought her into contact with the dress’s original wearer.
After the killing, the killer tidied the dress; she cares intensely about how the garment sits.
The original wearer had also been kept by the designer as a motionless mannequin; once the woman took the dress, she became the next one.

title: Wake Up
story:
The mother settled her daughter into the wheelchair and tucked the blanket around her.
The daughter’s eyes were open. When the mother touched her face, she even gave a slight shake of her head.
The mother laid that bandaged hand back on her lap and said softly, “When will you finally wake up?”
answer:
In this story there is an experimental device that can drive a person’s simple body movements through preset programs, but cannot restore consciousness. The daughter’s father ran a tech company and had taken part in developing it.
While swimming, the daughter’s hand had gotten caught in the drain at the bottom of the pool. Trapped for a long time, she was rescued but remained in a coma ever after; the wound on her hand was still bandaged. Unable to accept that she could only lie there, her mother insisted on fitting her with the device.
When it senses touch, the device makes the daughter raise her eyes, shake her head, and so on. The mother knows these responses come from a program, yet every day she lifts her daughter out of bed, tucks the blanket around her, and talks to her.
The daughter seems to respond to her mother, but her consciousness has never returned. What the mother hopes for is the day these movements truly come from the daughter herself.
hints: Open eyes and a shake of the head do not mean the daughter has regained consciousness.
In this story there is an experimental device that can only control body movements.
The responses to touch are preset in the device; the mother keeps hoping her daughter will one day answer on her own.

title: The Brooch
story:
My best friend was dead.
I told the police: the body had been moved; someone wanted to dress her death up as a suicide.
A brooch was found under the sofa. When the man was taken away, I smiled.
answer:
After the man broke up with her, my best friend killed herself at home, leaving a note. I was the one who found the note and her body first, so I knew how she had died; still, I laid all my bitterness at the man’s door.
I hid the note, moved the body, messed up the scene, and tossed a brooch the man had once left behind under the sofa. Then I called the police, claiming someone had killed my friend and then staged the scene as a suicide.
The brooch led the police to the man, who had been there before, and they took him in for questioning. Watching him being led away, I believed my revenge had worked, and I smiled.
I was the one who tampered with the body and the scene; the “homicide disguised as a suicide” was a story I was trying to sell to the police. The brooch proves nothing about him killing her.
hints: My best friend’s death did not happen the way I described it to the police.
The brooch had been left there long ago; I was the one who moved where it showed up.
After my friend’s suicide, I hid the note and altered the scene, trying to drag her ex-boyfriend into the investigation.

title: The Rusted Railing
story:
Halfway through their candlelit dinner, the couple fell from the balcony together.
The broken railing was covered in rust. The husband’s phone lay nearby; the last incoming call he had answered was labeled “Debt Collector.”
The run-down flat was one the husband had picked on purpose.
answer:
After going bankrupt, the husband felt he had failed his wife. Remembering the accident insurance he had bought with her as the beneficiary, he resolved to disguise his own death as an accident so that she could collect the payout.
He deliberately rented a worn-out high-rise flat with an aging balcony railing, and quietly kept weakening the railing, planning to fall from there. The wife knew nothing of his plan, but while tidying up she found the policy, and she too began to toy with the idea of killing her husband for the insurance money.
That night, the wife drugged the husband during the candlelit dinner. Using another SIM card, she called his phone, let the call connect, labeled the incoming number “Debt Collector,” and left the phone on the balcony, wanting people to believe he had met with an accident right after a call from debt collectors.
She dragged her unconscious husband to the railing, ready to push him over. The railing, already weakened by the husband himself, could not bear the strain of two bodies and snapped without warning. The wife lost her support and fell together with her husband.
The “accident” the husband had prepared to leave his wife was used by her, ahead of schedule, to kill him, and in the end it carried them both down.
hints: The husband picked this flat on purpose, and he had also tampered with that railing.
The “Debt Collector” label and the call itself were both arranged by the wife.
Both of them meant to turn the husband’s accidental death into insurance money, neither knowing the other already had a plan.

title: Multiple Choice
story:
I led the girl’s father into an empty house and pointed at the doors upstairs.
“Pick one. Your daughter is inside one of them.”
He deliberated for a long time.
In truth, whichever door he opened, he would find her.
answer:
I had kidnapped the girl, then lured her father into the house and set him this multiple-choice question.
The father believed his daughter was locked in one of the rooms, and that choosing the right door would let him take her home. He did not know I had already killed the girl and placed different parts of her body in every one of the rooms he could choose from.
So whichever door he chose, he would find a part of his daughter; and whichever door he chose, he could never bring home a living one.
hints: The father assumed he was looking for someone whole and alive.
Every room he can choose from truly contains something of his daughter’s.
The girl has been killed, and her body is spread across the rooms.

title: The Cliff-Top Fridge
story:
In the parking lot at the foot of the cliff lay the bodies of three men and a refrigerator.
One of those men had pushed the refrigerator over the edge just before he died.
answer:
A man came home to his house at the cliff’s edge and caught the scent of an unfamiliar perfume; he suspected his wife had brought her lover there. Looking down the cliff, he saw a stranger running across the parking lot and decided this was the lover making his escape.
Outside the house stood an empty refrigerator waiting to be hauled away. Furious, the man shoved it to the cliff’s edge and pushed it down toward the runner below. As he pushed it over, he lost his own balance and fell off the cliff.
The man crushed below was a mere passerby; the real lover, panicking, had hidden inside the empty refrigerator.
The husband, the mistaken passerby, and the lover hidden in the fridge all lay dead at the foot of the cliff.
hints: The man who pushed the refrigerator fell down himself.
The man running in the parking lot was mistaken for someone else; he had nothing to do with the wife.
The real lover was hiding inside the refrigerator and went over the cliff with it.

title: The Figure on the Balcony
story:
My home is on the eighteenth floor. Going to the bathroom in the middle of the night, I saw a stranger’s silhouette on the glass door to the balcony.
I meant to go wake Mom and Dad, took half a step, then quietly slipped back into my own bedroom instead.
My parents’ door was right over there. Yet I hid, and called the police on my phone.
answer:
A night light was on in the living room, the balcony outside was pitch dark, and the glass door mirrored the room’s interior.
At first I took the stranger for someone standing on the balcony. Turning to fetch my parents, I realized the figure in the glass came from inside the house: with his back to me, he stood at the mouth of the hallway leading to my parents’ bedroom, rummaging through a cabinet.
A burglar had gotten into our home. Reaching my parents’ room meant passing right beside him and risked alerting him. My own bedroom was just behind me, so while he had not noticed, I quietly backed into it, hid, and called the police from my phone.
What frightened me into hiding was realizing that the man in the glass was far closer than I had first thought.
hints: Outside it is pitch dark, and the glass door mirrors the lit room inside.
As I set out for my parents’ room, I realized the stranger stood right on the path I had to take.
What I saw was the intruder’s reflection inside the house; I backed into my own room nearby and called the police.

title: It’s Going to Spill
story:
The moment the car sped up, the woman pressed both hands to the top of her head.
“Slow down! It’s going to spill!”
As the driver slowed, she asked urgently, “Where is my lid?”
There was not a single drink in the car.
answer:
The woman had eaten wild mushrooms picked by mistake and been poisoned. Hallucinating, she believed she was a milkshake without a lid. Her family was rushing her to the hospital.
Whenever the car accelerated, she feared she would slosh over, pressed her hands on top of her head, and kept searching for a “cup lid” that could cover her. The drink she kept talking about was her own self.
hints: The car is rushing the woman to the hospital, and she is misreading what is happening to her.
The thing she fears will spill is herself.
After eating poisonous mushrooms, she hallucinated and took herself for a milkshake without a lid.

title: The Fourth Room
story:
I chased him into that house.
In the first room, the whole room was staring at me.
In the second, I felt myself being laughed at.
In the third, all those fingers pointed my way.
In the fourth, I finally found him.
Afterwards, I too stayed in that house.
answer:
After my family member vanished, I spent a long time tracking a man suspected of murder, until I finally found where he lived and, in my fury, stormed in alone.
The first three rooms were filled with his collection. The containers in the first held the victims’ eyes; the second preserved tongues, which my mind turned into mouths laughing at me; the third displayed hands taken from the victims, some of the fingers pointing toward the doorway.
There was no one living in those rooms. The “staring” and the “laughing” were how the collection felt to me in fear and rage.
The fourth room was where the killer himself lived. I failed to overpower him, and he killed me. My body, in turn, became part of the collection in that house.
hints: No one living is in the first three rooms; what is seen there comes from past victims.
The gazes, the mockery, and the accusations correspond to the eyes, the tongues, and the hands.
I broke alone into the killer’s collection rooms, was killed once I found him, and became the next piece of the collection.

title: One Hundred Million
story:
I thought it over for a long time before I finally spoke:
“I agree — one hundred million truly satisfies me.”
The money arrived.
A spider dropped onto me.
“Wò cào!” (a Chinese curse)
I died.
answer:
I had entered a supernatural deal: after receiving the one hundred million, every sentence I spoke for the rest of my life had to end rhyming with “yì,” the Chinese word for that sum (roughly the English “ee” sound); the moment I broke the rule, I would die.
I knew the rule. After weighing my words, I sealed the deal with “agree” and “me,” both ending in that sound, and the money really did arrive.
When the spider dropped onto me, the fright knocked the rule out of my head, and I blurted out “Wò cào!” That exclamation does not end with the rhyme, and the deal took my life on the spot.
hints: The money is real, but taking it attached a rule that never stops applying.
The rule governs the words spoken aloud; the spider only made me forget to follow it.
Every sentence I speak must end rhyming with “yì” (the “ee” sound); my startled cry broke the deal.

title: A Wall of Certificates
story: I came home with a new award certificate, planning to hang it on the wall. Dad, who used to beam at that wall of certificates, wore a look of gloom today. Mom, on the other hand, couldn’t stop grinning.
answer: I was an excellent student, and the walls of our home were covered with award certificates. Every time Dad looked at that wall he smiled, and I always believed he was proud of me. Then one day I brought home a new certificate, and when Mom pulled down the old ones to make room, she stumbled upon the private money Dad had hidden behind them. She gave him a furious scolding and confiscated the savings hidden across the whole wall, grinning from ear to ear; Dad, for all his painstaking scheming, had labored for nothing, and he could not help sighing over and over — a whole wall of secret savings, and he had never let himself spend a cent of it.
hints: When Dad looked at the certificates, part of what was on his mind was what lay behind them.
The new certificate needed room, so Mom took the old ones down.
Dad’s secret savings were hidden behind the old certificates, and Mom discovered and confiscated them along with those.

title: The Same Thing
story:
“Tonight I killed several zombies, vampires, and witches.
“They kept coming to my door, all of them carrying the same thing.
“It was only when I opened one of them and saw what was inside that I began to be afraid.
“The sirens are getting closer now.”
answer:
It was Halloween. People from around the neighborhood, dressed in monster costumes, were going door to door for candy, each carrying a candy basket.
I took the visitors for real zombies, vampires, and witches, and attacked and killed them. Only when I opened one of the baskets, saw the candy inside, and realized the monsters’ clothing was mere costume did I understand that I had killed human beings.
The sirens meant the police were closing in. I had believed I was wiping out monsters; now I saw that I had become a killer, and I began to be afraid.
hints: The people in different costumes were all doing the same thing, carrying containers that served the same purpose.
The baskets held candy, and that night was Halloween.
I mistook the trick-or-treaters for real monsters, and only recognized their costumes after I had killed them.

title: Regret
story:
She is getting married. The groom wears the face I used to have.
I once dated her, and I had imagined putting that ring on her finger myself.
But after the accident, whenever she saw me there was only fear.
At the wedding, I still sent them my blessing.
answer:
My twin brother and I fell for the same girl at the same time. Keeping it from her, we posed as one person and took turns dating her. She believed the boyfriend who came to see her each time was one and the same man.
Later I was in an accident that badly injured my face and changed my looks. The next time the girl saw me, before I could explain who I was, her face filled with fear and she backed away. She took me for a stranger.
I read that moment as proof she could not accept what I had become. I never told her the truth; I chose to bow out and let my brother carry on with her under that boyfriend’s identity.
In the end the girl married my brother, never knowing that the person who had dated her had really been two people. All I could do was carry the part of the past she knew nothing about, and send the two of them my blessing.
hints: The groom and I once looked exactly alike, but she never knew there had been two of us.
The accident changed my face, and when she saw me again she did not recognize me.
The twins took turns playing one and the same boyfriend; after I was injured I withdrew, and my brother carried the identity on.

title: The ‘Move Your Car’ Call
story:
My colleague said he was dropping out of the race, and insisted on buying me drinks.
That night, a ‘move your car’ phone call cost me my promotion.
Later, he made executive and brought his wife to meet me.
When I saw her face, I finally understood who had really stood that round of drinks.
answer:
My colleague and I were competing for the same management position. Before the results came out, he told me he was withdrawing and invited me out for drinks, and my guard came down.
Over the meal I received a call asking me to move my car. Sure I only had to nudge it a few feet in the parking lot, I drove after drinking — and hit another car. The woman at the wheel called the police, and the drunk-driving incident made the company strike me from the promotion.
The whole thing had been arranged by my colleague. He had his wife drive over and block my car in, then place the ‘move your car’ call to me; he himself kept me company over drinks, waiting for the point where, drunk, I would still decide to drive. His wife was right there waiting in the parking lot.
In the end my colleague won the promotion. When he brought his wife to meet me, I recognized the woman driver from that night’s collision — the one who had then called the police — and only then did I understand that the ‘I’m withdrawing’ drinks had been a trap from start to finish.
hints: When my colleague bought me those drinks, he had no real intention of withdrawing.
The ‘move your car’ call led drunk me straight into the driver’s seat.
The woman driver who called the police was my colleague’s wife, working with him in advance so that I would move my car after drinking.

title: Runs Hot and Cold
story:
Sometimes my wife is tender with me; sometimes she won’t let me touch her at all.
Her eating is strange too — left hand today, right hand tomorrow.
I could never make sense of it.
Until she said to me with a smile, “No more taking turns.”
That day, she killed me.
answer:
I believed I had one wife. In truth there was a pair of twin sisters, taking turns living with me under a single identity.
Since childhood the sisters had insisted on splitting everything equally, and after marriage they divided up even the time spent with me. They differed in temper and in their dominant hands, which is why my “wife’s” moods and table habits kept changing without my ever knowing the person had changed.
Later the two of them no longer wanted to take turns; each wanted her own share kept by her side forever. Together they killed me, divided my body into two portions, and each carried one away.
“No more taking turns” meant they had settled on a new way of splitting me between them.
hints: It wasn’t only my wife’s attitude that changed — her dominant hand changed too.
Two people were taking turns living under one identity, and I never noticed.
The twin sisters split their time with their husband equally; later they killed him and split his body instead.

title: The Final Beat
story:
When the music stopped, the audience still had their faces turned upward.
She took one step to the side.
No applause came; the screams arrived first.
She died.
answer:
She was a blind high-wire performer who judged her endpoint from sound cues given by the accompanist. At the end of the wire stood a platform, and she had an agreement with him: when she reached the platform, the music would stop, and she would step sideways onto it to close the show.
For this performance she wore no safety harness. While she was still midway along the wire, the power suddenly cut out and the accompaniment stopped. She took the unexpected silence for the agreed endpoint signal and took one step to the side.
There was no platform beside her yet. Her foot found nothing, and she fell. The audience watched with their faces turned up, unable to stop something that happened in an instant.
hints: The audience looked up because the performance was happening high off the ground.
The music stopping was itself a signal, telling her she could leave the wire.
The blind wire walker mistook the blackout’s silence for her arrival at the end, and stepped toward a platform that was not yet there.

title: The Lure
story:
He set the item on the table, and in that moment I decided to buy it.
Yet I kept asking about the price, and asked him to sit down and talk things over slowly.
Just as he was talking at his happiest, several men walked over and took him away.
They were the ones I had been waiting for all along.
answer:
My father was killed in a home invasion, and our heirloom jade pendant was stolen along with it. I had always wanted to recover the pendant and find the killer from that day.
I posted a high-priced wanted-to-buy listing online. This man contacted me, saying he had a similar jade pendant. When we met and he laid it on the table, I recognized the fine little scratch only family members knew about, and confirmed it was ours.
I quietly contacted the police, then kept haggling and kept him seated, stalling the deal until the officers arrived. The men who took him away were the police.
The pendant carried the lead into the investigation; the police then traced how it had passed into his hands and reopened the old case, confirming that he had taken part in that home invasion.
hints: My high-priced buying post was laid as bait, meant to draw out whoever held the item.
I had recognized it long before, yet I kept negotiating to drag out the time.
The pendant stolen when my father was killed had surfaced; I held the seller in place and waited for the police to arrive and investigate.

title: Such a Good Mimic
story:
Late at night, my screams always drew the neighbors in.
From the balcony there was another voice, crying out along with me, time after time.
My husband opened the door, gave a brief explanation, and the neighbors left with a laugh.
The moment the door shut, my husband came back to stand before me.
answer:
My husband had been beating me at home for a long time. On the balcony we kept a parrot; after hearing my screams so often, it had learned to cry out along with me. Both sounds had drawn the neighbors’ attention.
When someone knocked, my husband would stop, plant himself in the doorway, point at the parrot, and explain that it loved imitating sounds from the television — what they had just heard was only the bird. The parrot would let out the very same cry, making the story all the more convincing.
Under his threats, I dared not ask for help in front of him. The neighbors never saw my condition; they believed his explanation, took the whole thing for a misunderstanding, and left with a laugh.
The screams that might have brought help were smothered by the parrot’s mimicry. Once the door closed, the violence continued.
hints: The voice on the balcony could mimic me, but could not explain how the sound had been learned.
My husband used the parrot on the balcony to explain away my screams, and kept himself in the doorway blocking the neighbors’ view.
The abuse was real; once the parrot had learned my screams, my husband used it to keep up the appearance that no one at home was hurt.

title: Fireflies
story:
The car broke down, and Dad got out.
Where the headlights shone there were many small points of light. I wanted to go catch fireflies, but I couldn’t get the door beside me to open no matter how hard I pulled.
Dad suddenly ran off into the distance, and the points of light went with him.
I waited all night. He never came back.
answer:
At night, the car broke down on a remote mountain road, and the father got out to check it. His daughter, still very young, stayed in the back seat.
The father saw wolves closing in. Their eyes reflected the headlights, and through the window glass his daughter took the distant points of light for fireflies. She wanted to get out and catch them, so he locked the rear doors and left her inside the car.
He tried to draw the approaching wolves away from the car and ran off in another direction. The wolves chased after him and left, and all the daughter saw was the points of light moving away too.
After daybreak people found the car and rescued the daughter. The father, far away, was attacked by the wolves and never came back alive. All that night, the girl had no idea what her father was facing.
hints: The points of light were not glowing by themselves — they were reflecting the headlights.
After Dad locked the doors and ran into the distance, the points of light moved after him.
The ‘fireflies’ were wolves’ eyes; the father kept his daughter in the car and drew the wolves away himself.

title: The Boat Was Right There
story:
Five friends took a yacht out to sea, and after anchoring, one after another they jumped into the water.
The boat stayed right beside them the whole time.
A few hours later, all five were dead, and the boat was empty.
answer:
The weather was scorching, and after anchoring, all five couldn’t wait to jump in and cool off with a swim — forgetting to lower the boarding ladder stowed aboard.
The yacht’s gunwale was high and its hull smooth near the waterline, with nothing to grip or stand on. They tried again and again and never made it up; with everyone in the water, there was no one left to lower the ladder for the others.
Their communications gear and belongings were still on board, and the boat sat on open water far from anyone, so no rescue came in time. All five struggled beside the boat until their strength ran out, and they drowned one after another.
The boat that killed them stayed in sight the whole time; the only thing missing was a ladder that could have been let down from on board.
hints: All five had gone into the water; not a single person was left aboard.
The boat’s side was high and smooth, with no foothold they could grab.
The boarding ladder stayed stowed on the boat, and with everyone in the water there was no one to lower it.

title: The Promises
story:
In that high-rise by the sea, fifteen residents died one after another within a single month.
A woman took advantage of the falling prices to buy a sea-facing apartment, and handed the keys to her father.
A few days later, she walked into a police station and confessed that those residents had all died at her hand.
She said she had finally fulfilled her father’s two promises.
answer:
Father and daughter had once lived in a small cottage with a view of the sea. The father had promised that one day she would live in a big house overlooking the whole of it. Then a high-rise went up across from them and shut out their view.
He worked himself to the bone for a sea-facing apartment in that tower, but the money was never enough, and his body finally gave out. So the daughter decided to use murders to drive the building’s prices down. She killed fifteen residents one after another, turning the place into something people feared. When some owners grew desperate to sell, she was at last able to buy one of the apartments with her savings.
She handed the keys to her father. Learning that she had bought it right on the heels of a string of serial murders, he pressed her until she confessed everything. Already gravely ill, he could not live with what she had done, and before he died he made her promise to turn herself in.
After her father’s death, she carried out the final promise. The first promise was living in a big house facing the sea; the second was bearing the consequences of the crimes committed to obtain that home.
hints: The woman’s purchase was directly tied to the murders in the building.
Her father could never have afforded the apartment; the murders made some owners desperate to sell.
She killed to drive the prices down, and once her father learned of it, he left one last demand: turn yourself in.

title: The Crescent Moon
story:
Mother has grown old; it is my turn to go out and find food.
She always warned me to be careful of the man in the wolf skin.
I was caught and tied up beside the fire. The firelight lit up the crescent on my shoulder, and the man suddenly threw down his torch and untied me.
I lunged at him.
He never raised his gun; all that fell from his chest was a torn family photograph.
answer:
This is a fictional tale in which wolves understand humans and can raise human children. The mother who raised me was a wolf.
Ten years earlier, a hunter had killed the wolf king and had his skin made into a cloak. The wolf’s cubs later died in his traps as well.
